title.zh: 卷一百二十九 列傳第十七 Feng Sheng, Fu Youde, Liao Yongzhong, Yang Jing, Hu Mei
title.en: Volume 129 Biographies 17: Feng Sheng, Fu Youde, Liao Yongzhong, Yang Jing, Hu Mei
title.raw: 卷一百二十九 列傳第十七 Feng Sheng, Fu Youde, Liao Yongzhong, Yang Jing, Hu Mei Volume 129 Biographies 17: Feng Sheng, Fu Youde, Liao Yongzhong, Yang Jing, Hu Mei

sentences.zh: 馮勝，定遠人。

translations.literal: Feng Sheng was a man of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sheng was a native of Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 初名國勝，又名宗異，最後名勝。

translations.literal: His original name was Guosheng; he was also called Zongyi, and finally took the name Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was first named Guosheng, later called Zongyi, and finally took the name Sheng.

sentences.zh: 生時黑氣滿室，經日不散。

translations.literal: At his birth black vapor filled the room and did not disperse for a whole day.
translations.idiomatic: When he was born, black vapor filled the room and lingered for an entire day.

sentences.zh: 及長，雄勇多智略，與兄國用俱喜讀書，通兵法，元末結寨自保。

translations.literal: When grown, he was bold and brave and full of stratagems; he and his elder brother Guoyong both delighted in reading, mastered military strategy, and at the end of the Yuan fortified a stockade to protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was bold, brave, and resourceful. He and his elder brother Guoyong both loved books and mastered military strategy; in the closing years of the Yuan they fortified a stockade to defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 太祖略地至妙山，國用偕勝來歸，甚見親信。

translations.literal: When the Taizu was securing territory as far as Miaoshan, Guoyong came over with Sheng and was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu advanced as far as Miaoshan, Guoyong came over with Sheng and won his deep trust.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗從容詢天下大計，國用對曰：「金陵龍蟠虎踞，帝王之都，先拔之以為根本。

translations.literal: The Taizu once asked at leisure about the great plan for the realm, and Guoyong replied: "Jinling coils like a dragon and crouches like a tiger—the capital of emperors; seize it first as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu once asked him, in an unhurried conversation, about the grand strategy for the realm. Guoyong answered: "Jinling coils like a dragon and crouches like a tiger—it is an imperial capital. Take it first and make it your foundation.

sentences.zh: 然後四出征伐，倡仁義，收人心，勿貪子女玉帛，天下不足定也。」

translations.literal: Then campaign in all four directions, proclaim benevolence and righteousness, win men's hearts, and do not covet women, jade, or silks—the realm will not be hard to settle."
translations.idiomatic: Then march in all four directions, proclaim benevolence and righteousness, win the people's hearts, and do not covet women, jade, or silks, and the realm will not be hard to secure.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，俾居幕府，從克滁、和，戰三叉河、板門寨、雞籠山，皆有功。

translations.literal: The Taizu was greatly pleased and had him stay in the headquarters; he followed in the capture of Chu and He, and fought at San Cha River, Banmen Stockade, and Jilong Mountain, all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu was greatly pleased and kept him in headquarters. He followed the campaigns that took Chu and He and fought at San Cha River, Banmen Stockade, and Jilong Mountain, distinguishing himself in each.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，取太平，遂命國用典親兵，委以心腹。

translations.literal: He followed in crossing the Yangzi, took Taiping, and was then ordered to command the personal guard and entrusted as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi with the army and helped take Taiping, after which the Taizu put Guoyong in charge of the personal guard and treated him as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 太祖既擒陳野先，釋之，令招其部曲。

translations.literal: After the Taizu had captured Chen Yexian, he released him and ordered him to summon his followers.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taizu captured Chen Yexian, he released him and ordered him to rally his followers.

sentences.zh: 國用策其必叛，不如弗遣。

translations.literal: Guoyong judged that he would surely rebel and advised that he not be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Guoyong judged that Chen would surely rebel and advised against sending him.

sentences.zh: 尋果叛，為其下所殺，其從子兆先復擁眾屯方山。

translations.literal: Before long he did rebel and was killed by his subordinates; his nephew Zhaoxian again gathered troops and encamped at Fangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chen did rebel and was killed by his own men; his nephew Zhaoxian then rallied the troops and encamped at Fangshan.

sentences.zh: 蠻子海牙扼採石，國用與諸將攻破海牙水寨，又破擒兆先，盡降其眾三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Mansai Haiya held Caishi; Guoyong and the generals stormed Haiya's river stockade, then defeated and captured Zhaoxian, reducing all his more than thirty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Mansai Haiya held Caishi. Guoyong and the other generals stormed Haiya's river stockade, then defeated and captured Zhaoxian, bringing more than thirty thousand of his men to surrender.

sentences.zh: 眾疑懼，太祖擇驍勇者五百人為親軍，宿衛帳中。

translations.literal: The troops were suspicious and afraid; the Taizu chose five hundred fierce warriors as a personal guard to lodge in his tent.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were uneasy and afraid. The Taizu chose five hundred fierce warriors as a personal guard to lodge in his tent.

sentences.zh: 悉屏舊人，獨留國用侍榻側，五百人者始安。

translations.literal: He dismissed all the old followers and kept only Guoyong at his bedside; only then did the five hundred feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed all the old followers and kept only Guoyong at his bedside; only then did the five hundred feel reassured.

sentences.zh: 即命國用將之，以攻集慶，爭效死先登。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Guoyong to lead them in the attack on Jiqing, and they vied to die first in the assault.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately put Guoyong in command of them for the assault on Jiqing, and they vied to die in the van.

sentences.zh: 與諸將下鎮江、丹陽、甯國、泰興、宜興，從征金華，攻紹興，累擢親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: With the generals he reduced Zhenjiang, Danyang, Ningguo, Taixing, and Yixing; he followed the campaign on Jinhua and attacked Shaoxing, and was repeatedly promoted to commander of the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: With the other generals he took Zhenjiang, Danyang, Ningguo, Taixing, and Yixing, joined the campaign against Jinhua, and attacked Shaoxing, rising repeatedly until he became commander of the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 卒於軍，年三十六。

translations.literal: He died in the army at the age of thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died on campaign at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 太祖哭之慟。

translations.literal: The Taizu wept for him in deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu wept for him in deep grief.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年追封郢國公，肖像功臣廟，位第八。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ying; his portrait was placed in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers, in the eighth place.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ying; his portrait was placed in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers, in the eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 國用之卒，子誠幼，勝先已積功為元帥，遂命襲兄職，典親軍。

translations.literal: When Guoyong died, his son Cheng was young; Sheng had already accumulated merit as marshal, so he was ordered to succeed to his brother's post and command the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Guoyong died, his son Cheng was still young. Sheng had already won merit as a marshal, so he was ordered to succeed to his brother's post and command the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒逼龍灣。

translations.literal: Chen Youliang pressed upon Longwan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youliang pressed upon Longwan.

sentences.zh: 太祖禦之，戰石灰山。

translations.literal: The Taizu went out to meet him and fought at Shihui Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu went out to meet him and fought at Shihui Mountain.

sentences.zh: 勝攻其中堅，大破之，又追究破之採石，遂復太平。

translations.literal: Sheng struck their main force and routed them; he pursued and again defeated them at Caishi, then recovered Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng struck their main force and routed them, pursued them, and defeated them again at Caishi, then recovered Taiping.

sentences.zh: 從征友諒，破安慶水寨，長驅至江州，走友諒。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Youliang, stormed the Anqing river stockade, drove straight to Jiangzhou, and put Youliang to flight.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Youliang, stormed the Anqing river stockade, drove straight to Jiangzhou, and put Youliang to flight.

sentences.zh: 進親軍都護。

translations.literal: He was advanced to protector of the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to protector of the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 從解安豐圍，遷同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He followed in relieving the siege of Anfeng and was transferred to vice-director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He helped lift the siege of Anfeng and was appointed vice-director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 從戰鄱陽，下武昌，克廬州，移兵取江西諸路。

translations.literal: He fought at Poyang, took Wuchang, captured Luzhou, and shifted troops to seize the circuits of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Poyang, took Wuchang, captured Luzhou, and shifted troops to seize the circuits of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 與諸將收淮東，克海安壩，取泰州。

translations.literal: With the generals he recovered eastern Huai, captured Hai'an Dam, and took Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: With the other generals he recovered eastern Huai, captured Hai'an Dam, and took Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 徐達圍高郵未下，還師援宜興，以勝督軍。

translations.literal: Xu Da besieged Gaoyou but could not take it; he returned with the army to relieve Yixing, and Sheng was put in charge of the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da besieged Gaoyou without success, returned to relieve Yixing, and put Sheng in charge of the army.

sentences.zh: 高郵守將詐降，勝令指揮康泰帥數百人先入城，敵閉門盡殺之。

translations.literal: The Gaoyou garrison commander feigned surrender; Sheng ordered the commander Kang Tai to lead several hundred men into the city first, and the enemy shut the gates and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoyou garrison commander feigned surrender. Sheng ordered Commander Kang Tai to lead several hundred men into the city first, and the enemy shut the gates and slaughtered them.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，召勝決大杖十，令步詣高郵。

translations.literal: The Taizu was angry, summoned Sheng, and had him beaten with the great staff ten times, ordering him to go on foot to Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu was furious. He summoned Sheng, had him beaten ten strokes with the great staff, and ordered him to go on foot to Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 勝慚憤，攻甚力。

translations.literal: Sheng, ashamed and angry, pressed the assault fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed and angry, Sheng pressed the assault with great force.

sentences.zh: 達亦自宜興還，益兵攻克之，遂取淮安。

translations.literal: Da also returned from Yixing, reinforced the army, and captured it, then took Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da also returned from Yixing, reinforced the army, and captured the city, then took Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 安豐破，擒吳將呂珍於舊館。

translations.literal: When Anfeng fell, he captured the Wu general Lü Zhen at Jiuguan.
translations.idiomatic: When Anfeng fell, he captured the Wu general Lü Zhen at Jiuguan.

sentences.zh: 下湖州，克平江，功次平章常遇春，再遷右都督。

translations.literal: He reduced Huzhou and captured Pingjiang; his merit ranked second to the pingzhang Chang Yuchun, and he was again promoted to right commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He took Huzhou and captured Pingjiang. His merit ranked second only to the pingzhang Chang Yuchun, and he was promoted again to right commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍達北征，下山東諸州郡。

translations.literal: He followed the great general Da on the northern expedition and reduced the prefectures and districts of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the great general Xu Da on the northern expedition and reduced the prefectures and districts of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年兼太子右詹事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he also served as right tutor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 1 he also served as right tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 坐小法貶一官，為都督同知。

translations.literal: For a minor offense he was demoted one rank and made vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For a minor offense he was demoted one rank and made vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 引兵溯河，取汴、洛，下陝州，趨潼關。

translations.literal: He led troops upriver, took Bian and Luo, reduced Shanzhou, and pressed on Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops upriver, took Bian and Luoyang, reduced Shanzhou, and pressed on toward Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 守將宵遁，遂奪關，取華州。

translations.literal: The garrison commander fled by night, and he seized the pass and took Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander fled by night, so he seized the pass and took Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 還汴，謁帝行在。

translations.literal: He returned to Bian and paid homage at the emperor's traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Bian and paid homage at the emperor's traveling court.

sentences.zh: 授征虜右副將軍，留守汴梁。

translations.literal: He was appointed right vice general of the expedition against the barbarians and left to guard Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed right vice general of the northern expedition and left to guard Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 尋從大將軍征山西，由武陟取懷慶，逾太行，克碗子城，取澤、潞，擒元右丞賈成於猗氏。

translations.literal: Soon he followed the great general on the Shanxi campaign, took Huaqing by way of Wuzhi, crossed the Taihang, captured Wanzicheng, seized Ze and Lu, and captured the Yuan right censor-in-chief Jia Cheng at Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined the great general's campaign in Shanxi, took Huaqing by way of Wuzhi, crossed the Taihang range, captured Wanzicheng, seized Ze and Lu, and captured the Yuan right censor-in-chief Jia Cheng at Yishi.

sentences.zh: 克平陽、絳州，擒元左丞田保保等，獲將士五百餘人。

translations.literal: He captured Pingyang and Jiangzhou, seized the Yuan left censor-in-chief Tian Baobao and others, and took more than five hundred officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Pingyang and Jiangzhou, seized the Yuan left censor-in-chief Tian Baobao and others, and took more than five hundred officers and soldiers prisoner.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，詔右副將軍勝居常遇春下，偏將軍湯和居勝下，偏將軍楊璟居和下。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and ordered that the right vice general Sheng rank below Chang Yuchun, the lieutenant general Tang He below Sheng, and the lieutenant general Yang Jing below He.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and decreed that the right vice general Sheng should rank below Chang Yuchun, the lieutenant general Tang He below Sheng, and the lieutenant general Yang Jing below He.

sentences.zh: 二年渡河趨陝西，克鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the second year he crossed the river and pressed into Shaanxi, capturing Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he crossed the river into Shaanxi and captured Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 遂渡隴，取鞏昌，進逼臨洮，降李思齊。

translations.literal: He then crossed Long, took Gongchang, advanced on Lintao, and received the surrender of Li Siqi.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed Long, took Gongchang, advanced on Lintao, and received Li Siqi's surrender.

sentences.zh: 還從大將軍圍慶陽。

translations.literal: He returned and followed the great general in besieging Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and joined the great general in besieging Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 擴廓遣將攻原州，為慶陽聲援。

translations.literal: Köke Temür sent generals to attack Yuanzhou as a diversion for Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür sent generals to attack Yuanzhou to relieve pressure on Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 勝扼驛馬關敗其將，遂克慶陽，執張良臣。

translations.literal: Sheng held Yima Pass and defeated their generals, then captured Qingyang and took Zhang Liangchen prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng held Yima Pass, defeated their generals, captured Qingyang, and took Zhang Liangchen prisoner.

sentences.zh: 陝西悉平。

translations.literal: Shaanxi was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi was entirely pacified.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝召大將軍還，命勝駐慶陽，節制諸軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the emperor recalled the great general and ordered Sheng to remain at Qingyang and command all armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor recalled the great general and ordered Sheng to remain at Qingyang in command of all armies.

sentences.zh: 勝以關陝既定，輒引兵還。

translations.literal: Sheng, thinking that Guan and Shaan were already settled, forthwith led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking that Guan and Shaan were already settled, Sheng led the army back on his own.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，切責之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and sharply rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 念其功大，赦勿治。

translations.literal: Mindful of his great merit, he pardoned him and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his great merit, the emperor pardoned him and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 而賞賚金幣，不能半大將軍。

translations.literal: Yet the gold and silks he was granted could not reach half what the great general received.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the gold and silks he received amounted to less than half what the great general was given.

sentences.zh: 明年正月復以右副將軍同大將軍出西安，搗定西，破擴廓帖木兒，獲士馬數萬。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he again served as right vice general with the great general, marching out from Xi'an, striking into Dingxi, defeating Köke Temür, and capturing tens of thousands of men and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year he again served as right vice general alongside the great general, marching out from Xi'an, striking into Dingxi, defeating Köke Temür, and capturing tens of thousands of men and horses.

sentences.zh: 分兵自徽州南出一百八渡，徇略陽，擒元平章蔡琳，遂入沔州。

translations.literal: He detached troops south from Huizhou by the One Hundred and Eight Fords, overran Lüeyang, captured the Yuan pingzhang Cai Lin, and then entered Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He detached troops south from Huizhou by the One Hundred and Eight Fords, overran Lüeyang, captured the Yuan pingzhang Cai Lin, and then entered Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣別將自連雲棧取興元，移兵吐番，征哨極於西北。

translations.literal: He sent another general by the Lianyun plank road to take Xingyuan, shifted troops into Tibet, and pushed scouting parties to the farthest northwest.
translations.idiomatic: He sent another general by the Lianyun plank road to take Xingyuan, shifted troops into Tibet, and pushed scouting parties to the farthest northwest.

sentences.zh: 凱旋，論功授開國輔運推誠宣力武臣、特進榮祿大夫、右柱國、同參軍國事，封宋國公，食祿三千石，予世券。

translations.literal: On his triumphant return, for merit he was granted the titles founding martial minister who assists the state, promotes sincerity, and extends effort; specially advanced grand master of glorious emolument; right pillar of the state; and co-participant in state affairs; enfeoffed as Duke of Song with an income of three thousand piculs and given a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: On his triumphant return he was rewarded with the titles founding martial minister who assists the state, promotes sincerity, and extends effort; specially advanced grand master of glorious emolument; right pillar of the state; and co-participant in state affairs; enfeoffed as Duke of Song with an income of three thousand piculs and granted a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 誥詞謂勝兄弟親同骨肉，十餘年間，除肘腑之患，建爪牙之功，平定中原，佐成混一。

translations.literal: The patent of appointment said that the Feng brothers were as close as flesh and bone; for more than ten years they had removed troubles at the elbow and armpit, built the merit of fang and talon, pacified the Central Plain, and assisted in achieving unification.
translations.idiomatic: The patent of appointment said the Feng brothers were as close as flesh and bone; for more than ten years they had removed dangers at the emperor's side, built the merit of loyal arms, pacified the Central Plain, and helped achieve unification.

sentences.zh: 所以稱揚之者甚至。

translations.literal: The praise accorded them was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The praise heaped upon them was extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 五年，以勝宣力四方，與魏國公達、曹國公文忠各賜彤弓。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because Sheng had extended his strength in all four directions, he and the Duke of Wei Da and the Duke of Cao Wenzhong were each granted a red bow.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, because Sheng had extended his strength in all four directions, he and the Duke of Wei Xu Da and the Duke of Cao Li Wenzhong were each granted a red bow.

sentences.zh: 擴廓在和林，數擾邊。

translations.literal: Köke Temür was at Karakorum and repeatedly harassed the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür was at Karakorum and repeatedly harassed the frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝患之，大發兵三道出塞。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled by this and raised a great army in three columns beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was troubled by this and raised a great army in three columns beyond the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 命勝為征西將軍，帥副將軍陳德、傅友德等出西道，取甘肅。

translations.literal: Sheng was appointed general of the western expedition and led the vice generals Chen De, Fu Youde, and others on the western route to take Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was appointed general of the western expedition and led the vice generals Chen De, Fu Youde, and others on the western route to take Gansu.

sentences.zh: 至蘭州，友德以驍騎前驅，再敗元兵，勝復敗之掃林山。

translations.literal: At Lanzhou, Youde led fierce cavalry as vanguard and twice defeated Yuan troops; Sheng again defeated them at Saolin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At Lanzhou, Fu Youde led fierce cavalry as vanguard and twice defeated Yuan troops; Sheng defeated them again at Saolin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 至甘肅，元將上都驢迎降。

translations.literal: At Gansu, the Yuan general Shangdu Lü came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Gansu, the Yuan general Shangdu Lü came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 至亦集乃路，守將卜顏帖木兒亦降。

translations.literal: At the Yijinai circuit the garrison commander Buyan Temür also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yijinai circuit the garrison commander Buyan Temür also surrendered.

sentences.zh: 次別篤山，岐王朵兒只班遁去，追獲其平章長加奴等二十七人及馬駝牛羊十余萬。

translations.literal: Next at Biedu Mountain the Prince of Qi Du'erzhiban fled; they pursued and captured his pingzhang Changjianu and twenty-seven others, along with more than one hundred thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Next at Biedu Mountain the Prince of Qi Du'erzhiban fled. They pursued him and captured his pingzhang Changjianu and twenty-seven others, along with more than one hundred thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 是役也，大將軍達軍不利，左副將軍文忠殺傷相當，獨勝斬獲甚眾，全師而還。

translations.literal: In this campaign the great general Da's army fared badly, the left vice general Wenzhong's casualties were about even, and only Sheng killed and captured in great numbers and returned with the whole army intact.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign the great general Xu Da's army fared badly and the left vice general Li Wenzhong's casualties were about even, but Sheng alone killed and captured in great numbers and returned with his whole army intact.

sentences.zh: 會有言其私匿駝馬者，賞不行。

translations.literal: Just then someone said he had privately hidden camels and horses, and his reward was withheld.
translations.idiomatic: Just then someone accused him of privately hoarding camels and horses, and his reward was withheld.

sentences.zh: 自後數出練兵臨清、北平，出大同征元遺眾，鎮陝西及河南。

translations.literal: Afterward he repeatedly went out to drill troops at Linqing and Beiping, marched from Datong against Yuan remnants, and guarded Shaanxi and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he repeatedly went out to drill troops at Linqing and Beiping, marched from Datong against Yuan remnants, and guarded Shaanxi and Henan.

sentences.zh: 冊其女為周王妃。

translations.literal: His daughter was ennobled as consort to the Prince of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was ennobled as consort to the Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，大將軍達、左副將軍文忠皆卒，而元太尉納哈出擁眾數十萬屯金山，數為遼東邊害。

translations.literal: After a long while the great general Da and the left vice general Wenzhong both died, while the Yuan grand guardian Naghachu held several hundred thousand men encamped at Jinshan and repeatedly harmed the Liaodong frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the great general Xu Da and the left vice general Li Wenzhong both died, while the Yuan grand guardian Naghachu held several hundred thousand men at Jinshan and repeatedly raided the Liaodong frontier.

sentences.zh: 二十年命勝為征虜大將軍，穎國公傅友德、永昌侯藍玉為左右副將軍，帥南雄侯趙庸等以步騎二十萬征之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Sheng was appointed great general of the expedition against the barbarians, with the Duke of Ying Fu Youde and the Marquis of Yongchang Lan Yu as left and right vice generals, leading the Marquis of Nanxiong Zhao Yong and others with two hundred thousand infantry and cavalry against him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 Sheng was appointed great general of the northern expedition, with the Duke of Ying Fu Youde and the Marquis of Yongchang Lan Yu as left and right vice generals, leading the Marquis of Nanxiong Zhao Yong and others with two hundred thousand infantry and cavalry against him.

sentences.zh: 鄭國公常茂、曹國公李景隆、申國公鄧鎮等皆從。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zheng Chang Mao, the Duke of Cao Li Jinglong, the Duke of Shen Deng Zhen, and others all followed.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zheng Chang Mao, the Duke of Cao Li Jinglong, the Duke of Shen Deng Zhen, and others all accompanied the expedition.

sentences.zh: 帝復遣故所獲納哈出部將乃剌吾者奉璽書往諭降。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Nailawu, a former subordinate of Naghachu whom he had captured, bearing an imperial letter to urge surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Nailawu, a former subordinate of Naghachu whom he had captured, bearing an imperial letter to urge surrender.

sentences.zh: 勝出松亭關，分築大寧、寬河、會州、富峪四城。

translations.literal: Sheng marched out through Songting Pass and built in succession the four cities of Daning, Kuanhe, Huizhou, and Fuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng marched out through Songting Pass and built the four cities of Daning, Kuanhe, Huizhou, and Fuyu.

sentences.zh: 駐大寧逾兩月，留兵五萬守之，而以全師壓金山。

translations.literal: He remained at Daning for more than two months, left fifty thousand troops to guard it, and pressed on with the whole army toward Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at Daning for more than two months, left fifty thousand troops to guard it, and pressed on with the whole army toward Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 納哈出見乃剌吾驚曰：「爾尚存乎！」

translations.literal: When Naghachu saw Nailawu he exclaimed in surprise: "You are still alive!"
translations.idiomatic: When Naghachu saw Nailawu he exclaimed in surprise, "You are still alive!"

sentences.zh: 乃剌吾述帝恩德。

translations.literal: Nailawu recounted the emperor's kindness and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Nailawu recounted the emperor's kindness and virtue.

sentences.zh: 納哈出喜，遣其左丞、探馬赤等獻馬，且覘勝軍。

translations.literal: Naghachu was pleased and sent his left censor and the scout Temür and others to present horses and also to reconnoiter Sheng's army.
translations.idiomatic: Naghachu was pleased and sent his left censor and the scout Temür and others to present horses and also to reconnoiter Sheng's army.

sentences.zh: 勝已深入，逾金山，至女直苦屯，降納哈出之將全國公觀童。

translations.literal: Sheng had already advanced deep inland, crossed Jinshan, reached the Jurchen post of Kutun, and received the surrender of Naghachu's general, the Duke of the Whole Realm Guan Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had already advanced deep inland, crossed Jinshan, reached the Jurchen post of Kutun, and received the surrender of Naghachu's general, the Duke of the Whole Realm Guan Tong.

sentences.zh: 大軍奄至，納哈出度不敵，因乃剌吾請降。

translations.literal: The great army suddenly arrived; Naghachu judged that he could not resist and, through Nailawu, asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The great army suddenly arrived. Naghachu judged that he could not resist and, through Nailawu, asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 勝使藍玉輕騎受之。

translations.literal: Sheng sent Lan Yu with light cavalry to receive the surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent Lan Yu with light cavalry to receive the surrender.

sentences.zh: 玉飲納哈出酒，歡甚，解衣衣之。

translations.literal: Yu drank wine with Naghachu and was very merry; he took off his own garment and clothed him in it.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Yu drank wine with Naghachu and grew very merry; he took off his own garment and clothed Naghachu in it.

sentences.zh: 納哈出不肯服，顧左右咄咄語，謀遁去。

translations.literal: Naghachu would not submit; he turned to those beside him and spoke sharply, plotting to slip away.
translations.idiomatic: Naghachu would not submit. He turned to those beside him and spoke sharply, plotting to slip away.

sentences.zh: 勝之婿常茂在坐，遽起砍其臂。

translations.literal: Sheng's son-in-law Chang Mao was present; he sprang up at once and hacked off Naghachu's arm.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's son-in-law Chang Mao was present; he sprang up at once and hacked off Naghachu's arm.

sentences.zh: 都督耿忠擁以見勝。

translations.literal: The commander Geng Zhong seized him and brought him before Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Geng Zhong seized him and brought him before Sheng.

sentences.zh: 納哈出將士妻子十余萬屯松花河，聞納哈出傷，驚潰。

translations.literal: More than one hundred thousand of Naghachu's officers, soldiers, wives, and children were encamped on the Songhua River; when they heard that Naghachu was wounded, they panicked and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: More than one hundred thousand of Naghachu's officers, soldiers, wives, and children were encamped on the Songhua River. When they heard that Naghachu was wounded, they panicked and scattered.

sentences.zh: 勝遣觀童諭之乃降，得所部二十余萬人，牛羊馬駝輜重互百餘里。

translations.literal: Sheng sent Guan Tong to instruct them, and they then surrendered; he obtained more than two hundred thousand of their followers, and cattle, sheep, horses, camels, and baggage stretched for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent Guan Tong to instruct them, and they then surrendered. He obtained more than two hundred thousand of their followers, and cattle, sheep, horses, camels, and baggage stretched for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 還至亦迷河，復收其殘卒二萬余、車馬五萬。

translations.literal: On the return to the Yimi River he again gathered more than twenty thousand of their remnant troops and fifty thousand carts and horses.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to the Yimi River he again gathered more than twenty thousand remnant troops and fifty thousand carts and horses.

sentences.zh: 而都督濮英殿后，為敵所殺。

translations.literal: But the commander Pu Ying brought up the rear and was killed by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: But Commander Pu Ying brought up the rear and was killed by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 師還，以捷聞，並奏常茂激變狀，盡將降眾二十萬人入關。

translations.literal: When the army returned, victory was reported, and the incident in which Chang Mao had provoked the disturbance was also reported; all two hundred thousand of the surrendered masses were brought inside the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, victory was reported along with an account of how Chang Mao had provoked the disturbance. All two hundred thousand of the surrendered people were brought inside the passes.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，使使者迎勞勝等，械系茂。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and sent envoys to welcome and reward Sheng and the others; Mao was put in fetters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and sent envoys to welcome and reward Sheng and the others. Chang Mao was put in fetters.

sentences.zh: 會有言勝多匿良馬，使閽者行酒于納哈出之妻求大珠異寶，王子死二日強娶其女，失降附心，又失濮英三千騎，而茂亦訐勝過。

translations.literal: Just then someone said Sheng had hidden many fine horses, sent a gatekeeper to offer wine to Naghachu's wife to seek great pearls and rare treasures, and forcibly married her daughter two days after a prince's death, losing the hearts of those who had surrendered; he had also lost three thousand of Pu Ying's cavalry, and Mao also denounced Sheng's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Just then someone reported that Sheng had hidden many fine horses, sent a gatekeeper to offer wine to Naghachu's wife while seeking great pearls and rare treasures, and forcibly married her daughter two days after a prince's death, alienating those who had surrendered. He had also lost three thousand of Pu Ying's cavalry, and Chang Mao denounced his faults as well.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，收勝大將軍印，命就第鳳陽，奉朝請，諸將士亦無賞。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, took back Sheng's great general's seal, ordered him to retire to his estate at Fengyang and attend court by invitation only, and the officers and soldiers also received no reward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry. He took back Sheng's great general's seal, ordered him to retire to his estate at Fengyang and attend court by invitation only, and the officers and soldiers received no reward either.

sentences.zh: 勝自是不復將大兵矣。

translations.literal: From then on Sheng no longer commanded great armies.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Sheng never again commanded a great army.

sentences.zh: 二十一年奉詔調東昌番兵征曲靖。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he received orders to mobilize the Eastern Chang tribal troops for the campaign against Qujing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 he received orders to mobilize the Eastern Chang tribal troops for the campaign against Qujing.

sentences.zh: 番兵中道叛，勝鎮永甯撫安之。

translations.literal: The tribal troops rebelled on the march; Sheng remained at Yongning to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal troops rebelled en route, and Sheng remained at Yongning to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 二十五年命籍太原、平陽民為軍，立衛屯田。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was ordered to register the people of Taiyuan and Pingyang as soldiers and establish garrison colonies.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 he was ordered to register the people of Taiyuan and Pingyang as soldiers and establish garrison colonies.

sentences.zh: 皇太孫立，加太子太師，偕潁國公友德練軍山西、河南，諸公、侯皆聽節制。

translations.literal: When the imperial great-grandson was installed, Sheng was made grand tutor to the crown prince; together with the Duke of Ying Youde he drilled troops in Shanxi and Henan, and all the dukes and marquises were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial great-grandson was installed, Sheng was made grand tutor to the crown prince. Together with the Duke of Ying Fu Youde he drilled troops in Shanxi and Henan, and all the dukes and marquises were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 時詔列勳臣望重者八人，勝居第三。

translations.literal: At that time an edict listed eight meritorious ministers of high standing; Sheng ranked third.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court named eight eminent merit subjects; Feng Sheng ranked third.

sentences.zh: 太祖春秋高，多猜忌。

translations.literal: Taizu was advanced in years and much given to suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was growing old and increasingly suspicious.

sentences.zh: 勝功最多，數以細故失帝意。

translations.literal: Sheng's achievements were the greatest, yet repeatedly for minor matters he lost the emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sheng had earned the most merit, yet time and again petty incidents cost him the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 藍玉誅之月，召還京。

translations.literal: In the month when Lan Yu was executed, he was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The month Lan Yu was put to death, he was summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 逾二年，賜死，諸子皆不得嗣。

translations.literal: After more than two years, he was granted death; none of his sons was permitted to inherit his title.
translations.idiomatic: More than two years later he was ordered to take his own life, and none of his sons was allowed to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 而國用子誠積戰功雲南，累官至右軍左都督。

translations.literal: Yet Guoyong's son Zicheng accumulated battle merit in Yunnan and rose through repeated promotions to Left Vice Commander of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: Guoyong's son Zicheng, however, earned his way up in Yunnan through repeated battle service, eventually reaching the post of Left Vice Commander of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 納哈出者，元木華黎裔孫，為太平路萬戶。

translations.literal: Nahachu was a descendant of Muqali of the Yuan and served as myriarch of Taiping Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Nahachu was a descendant of the Yuan general Muqali and held the post of myriarch of Taiping Circuit.

sentences.zh: 太祖克太平被執，以名臣後，待之厚。

translations.literal: When Taizu captured Taiping, Nahachu was taken prisoner; as the scion of a noted minister, he was treated generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took Taiping, Nahachu was captured; as the heir of an eminent minister's house, he was treated with great favor.

sentences.zh: 知其不忘元，資遣北歸。

translations.literal: Knowing that he had not forgotten the Yuan, the court supplied him with resources and sent him back north.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he still held loyalty to the Yuan, the emperor furnished him with supplies and allowed him to return north.

sentences.zh: 元既亡，納哈出聚兵金山，畜牧蕃盛。

translations.literal: After the Yuan perished, Nahachu gathered troops at Jinshan, where his herds flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Yuan had fallen, Nahachu rallied forces at Jinshan and raised vast herds there.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使招諭之，終不報。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to summon and instruct him, but in the end he never responded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to win him over, but he never answered.

sentences.zh: 數犯遼東，為葉旺所敗。

translations.literal: He repeatedly raided Liaodong and was defeated by Ye Wang.
translations.idiomatic: He raided Liaodong again and again until Ye Wang defeated him.

sentences.zh: 勝等大兵臨之，乃降，封海西侯。

translations.literal: When Sheng and others brought a great army against him, he then submitted and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Haixi.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Sheng and the others marched on him in force, he surrendered and was created Marquis of Haixi.

sentences.zh: 從傅友德征雲南，道卒。

translations.literal: He followed Fu Youde on the campaign against Yunnan and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Fu Youde's expedition to Yunnan but died en route.

sentences.zh: 子察罕，改封瀋陽侯，坐藍玉黨死。

translations.literal: His son Chaghan was reassigned as Marquis of Shenyang and, implicated as a member of Lan Yu's faction, was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chaghan was reassigned the title Marquis of Shenyang but was executed for ties to Lan Yu's clique.

sentences.zh: 傅友德

translations.literal: Fu Youde
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youde

sentences.zh: 傅友德，其先宿州人，後徙碭山。

translations.literal: Fu Youde's ancestors were from Suzhou; later the family moved to Dangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youde's family originally came from Suzhou and later relocated to Dangshan.

sentences.zh: 元末從劉福通党李喜喜入蜀。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he followed Li Xixi, a partisan of Liu Futong, into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years of the Yuan he followed Liu Futong's follower Li Xixi into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 喜喜敗，從明玉珍，玉珍珍不能用。

translations.literal: When Xixi was defeated, he joined Ming Yuzhen, whom Yuzhen could not employ to advantage.
translations.idiomatic: After Xixi was beaten, he served Ming Yuzhen, who never found a good use for his talents.

sentences.zh: 走武昌，從陳友諒，無所知名。

translations.literal: He fled to Wuchang and followed Chen Youliang, but won no renown.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Wuchang and entered Chen Youliang's service, yet remained unknown.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻江州，至小孤山，友德帥所部降。

translations.literal: When Taizu attacked Jiangzhou and reached Little Gushan, Youde led his troops in submission.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu attacked Jiangzhou and reached Little Gushan, Fu Youde brought his command in and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝與語，奇之，用為將。

translations.literal: The emperor spoke with him and marveled at him, then employed him as a general.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu spoke with him, was struck by his ability, and made him a commander.

sentences.zh: 從常遇春援安豐，略廬州。

translations.literal: He followed Chang Yuchun in relieving Anfeng and raided Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chang Yuchun to relieve Anfeng and raided Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，從戰鄱陽湖，輕舟挫友諒前鋒。

translations.literal: On his return he fought at Poyang Lake, where in light boats he broke Youliang's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he fought at Poyang Lake and, in light craft, smashed Chen Youliang's vanguard.

sentences.zh: 被數創，戰益力，復與諸將邀擊于涇江口，友諒敗死。

translations.literal: Though wounded many times, he fought all the harder; he again joined the generals in an ambush at the mouth of the Jing River, and Youliang was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded repeatedly, he fought all the harder; he joined the other generals in an ambush at the Jing River mouth, and Chen Youliang was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 從征武昌，城東南高冠山下瞰城中，漢兵據之，諸將相顧莫前。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign on Wuchang; southeast of the city Crown Mountain rose high and overlooked the town, and the Han troops held it—the generals looked at one another and none advanced.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign on Wuchang, Crown Mountain southeast of the city commanded the town, and Han forces held it; the generals hesitated, and none would go forward.

sentences.zh: 友德帥數百人，一鼓奪之。

translations.literal: Youde led several hundred men and seized it in a single assault.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youde led several hundred men and took it in one rush.

sentences.zh: 流矢中頰洞脅，不為沮。

translations.literal: A stray arrow pierced his cheek and opened his flank, yet he was not dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow pierced his cheek and tore into his side, but he did not falter.

sentences.zh: 武昌平，授雄武衛指揮使。

translations.literal: When Wuchang was pacified, he was appointed commander of the Heroic Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchang fell, he was made commander of the Heroic Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 從徐達拔廬州，別將克夷陵、衡州、襄陽。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in taking Luzhou and, as a separate commander, captured Yiling, Hengzhou, and Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in capturing Luzhou and, in a separate column, took Yiling, Hengzhou, and Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 攻安陸，被九創，破擒其將任亮。

translations.literal: In the attack on Anlu he received nine wounds, broke the enemy, and captured their general Ren Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At Anlu he took nine wounds, routed the defenders, and captured the general Ren Liang.

sentences.zh: 從大軍下淮東，破張士誠援兵于馬騾港，獲戰艘千，復大破元將竹貞于安豐。

translations.literal: He followed the main army down the Huai east, defeated Zhang Shicheng's relief troops at Maluan Harbor and seized a thousand war vessels, and again heavily defeated the Yuan general Zhuzhen at Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with the main force down the eastern Huai, destroyed Zhang Shicheng's relief force at Maluan Harbor and took a thousand warships, then routed the Yuan general Zhuzhen at Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 同陸聚守徐州，擴廓遣將李二來攻，次陵子村。

translations.literal: Together with Lu Ju he defended Xuzhou; Köke Temür sent the general Li Er to attack, and he halted at Lingzi Village.
translations.idiomatic: With Lu Ju he held Xuzhou when Köke Temür sent General Li Er against it; Li Er camped at Lingzi Village.

sentences.zh: 友德度兵寡不敵，遂堅壁不戰。

translations.literal: Youde judged that his troops were too few to match the enemy and therefore strengthened his walls and did not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youde reckoned his force too small to meet the enemy head-on and held his walls without fighting.

sentences.zh: 詗其眾方散掠，以二千人溯河至呂梁，登陸擊之，單騎奮槊刺其將韓乙。

translations.literal: He reconnoitered that their host was scattered in looting, then with two thousand men went upriver to Lüliang, landed, and struck them; alone on horseback he charged with his spear and stabbed their general Han Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the enemy was scattered on plunder, he took two thousand men upriver to Lüliang, landed, and attacked; riding alone, he drove his spear into their general Han Yi.

sentences.zh: 敵敗去。

translations.literal: The enemy were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 度且復至，亟還，開城門而陣於野，臥戈以待，約聞鼓即起。

translations.literal: Judging that they would soon return, he hurried back, opened the city gates, and drew up in battle order in the open field, laying spears flat to wait, with orders to rise at the sound of the drum.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting them back soon, he raced to the city, threw open the gates, and formed up in the field with weapons laid flat, ready to spring up at the drum.

sentences.zh: 李二果至，鳴鼓，士騰躍搏戰，破擒二。

translations.literal: Li Er did indeed come; at the drum the men leapt up and fought hand to hand, defeating and capturing Er.
translations.idiomatic: Li Er returned as expected; at the drum his men leapt up and fought at close quarters, defeating and capturing him.

sentences.zh: 召還，進江淮行省參知政事，撤御前麾蓋，鼓吹送歸第。

translations.literal: He was recalled and advanced to administrative vice commissioner of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat; the imperial canopy and guard of honor were withdrawn, and drums and pipes escorted him home.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was promoted to administrative vice commissioner of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat; the imperial canopy and guard were withdrawn, and he was sent home to the beat of drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 明年從大將軍北征，破沂州，下青州。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the great general on the northern expedition, took Yizhou, and reduced Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined the great general's northern campaign, captured Yizhou, and took Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元丞相也速來援，以輕騎誘敵入伏，奮擊敗走之。

translations.literal: The Yuan chancellor Ayush came to relieve them; with light cavalry he lured the enemy into an ambush and, striking fiercely, defeated and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan chancellor Ayush came to relieve the city, Fu Youde lured the enemy into an ambush with light cavalry and drove them off in a fierce attack.

sentences.zh: 遂取萊陽、東昌。

translations.literal: He then took Laiyang and Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured Laiyang and Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 明年從定汴、洛，收諸山寨。

translations.literal: The next year he followed in securing Bian and Luo and in reducing the mountain stockades.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he helped secure Kaifeng and Luoyang and reduce the mountain strongholds.

sentences.zh: 渡河取衛輝、彰德，至臨清，獲元將為嚮導，取德州、滄州。

translations.literal: Crossing the river he took Weihui and Zhangde; reaching Linqing, he obtained Yuan generals as guides and took Dezhou and Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yellow River and took Weihui and Zhangde; at Linqing he secured Yuan generals as guides and seized Dezhou and Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 既克元都，偵邏古北隘口，守盧溝橋，略大同，還下保定、真定，守定州。

translations.literal: After the Yuan capital was taken, he reconnoitered the Gubeikou pass, held the Lugou Bridge, raided Datong, then returned to reduce Baoding and Zhending and garrisoned Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuan capital fell, he scouted the Gubeikou pass, held the Lugou Bridge, raided Datong, then swung back to take Baoding and Zhending and garrisoned Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 從攻山西，克太原。

translations.literal: He followed in the attack on Shanxi and took Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the assault on Shanxi and captured Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 擴廓自保安來援，萬騎突至。

translations.literal: Köke Temür came from Bao'an to relieve the city, and ten thousand horsemen suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür marched from Bao'an to relieve the city with ten thousand horsemen who burst upon them.

sentences.zh: 友德以五十騎沖卻之，因夜襲其營。

translations.literal: Youde with fifty horsemen charged and drove them back, then by night raided their camp.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youde charged them with fifty horsemen and threw them back, then raided their camp that night.

sentences.zh: 擴廓倉卒遁去，追至土門關，獲其士馬萬計。

translations.literal: Köke Temür fled in haste; they pursued to Tumen Pass and captured his troops and horses by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür fled in disarray; they pursued to Tumen Pass and took tens of thousands of his men and horses.

sentences.zh: 復敗賀宗哲于石州，敗脫列伯于宣府，遂西會大將軍，圍慶陽，以偏師駐靈州，遏其援兵，遂克慶陽。

translations.literal: He again defeated He Zongzhe at Shizhou and Töle Buqa at Xuanfu, then went west to join the great general, besieged Qingyang, and with a detached force garrisoned Lingzhou to block relief troops, thereby taking Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated He Zongzhe at Shizhou and Töle Buqa at Xuanfu, then marched west to join the great general, besieged Qingyang, and with a detached column held Lingzhou to block reinforcements until Qingyang fell.

sentences.zh: 還，賜白金文綺。

translations.literal: On his return he was granted white gold and patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he received gifts of white gold and brocade.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年從大將軍搗定西，大破擴廓。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he followed the great general in a thrust against Dingxi and heavily defeated Köke Temür.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 he joined the great general's strike into Dingxi and routed Köke Temür.

sentences.zh: 移兵伐蜀，領前鋒出一百八渡，奪略陽關，遂入沔。

translations.literal: He shifted troops to attack Shu, led the vanguard out through the One Hundred and Eight Fords, seized Liaoyang Pass, and entered Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Shu, he led the vanguard through the One Hundred and Eight Fords, took Liaoyang Pass, and entered Hanzhong territory at Mian.

sentences.zh: 分兵自連雲棧合攻漢中，克之。

translations.literal: He divided his force to attack Hanzhong by the Lianyun Plank Road in concert and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a column along the Lianyun Plank Road to join the assault on Hanzhong and captured it.

sentences.zh: 以饋餉不繼，還軍西安。

translations.literal: Because supplies did not keep up, he withdrew the army to Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: When supplies failed, he pulled the army back to Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 蜀將吳友仁寇漢中。

translations.literal: The Shu general Wu Youren raided Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu general Wu Youren attacked Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 友德以三千騎救之，攻鬥山寨，令軍中人燃十炬布山上，蜀兵驚遁。

translations.literal: Youde with three thousand horsemen went to its relief, fought at Mount Doudou, and ordered every man in the army to light ten torches on the mountain; the Shu troops fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youde rode to the rescue with three thousand cavalry, fought at Mount Doudou, and had each soldier light ten torches on the hills; the Shu army fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 是冬，論功授開國輔運推誠宣力武臣、榮祿大夫、柱國、同知大都督府事，封穎川侯，食祿千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: That winter, for merit he was made founding supporter who assists the enterprise, promotes sincerity and extends force, martial minister, Grand Master of Splendid Emolument, Pillar of the State, vice commissioner of the Chief Military Commission, and Marquis of Yingchuan with an emolument of fifteen hundred piculs and a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: That winter his service was rewarded with the titles founding supporter who assists the enterprise, promotes sincerity and extends force, martial minister, Grand Master of Splendid Emolument, and Pillar of the State; he became vice commissioner of the Chief Military Commission, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yingchuan with fifteen hundred piculs of grain, and received a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 明年充征虜前將軍，與征西將軍湯和分道伐蜀。

translations.literal: The next year he served as forward general of the expedition against the northern barbarians and, with the western expedition general Tang He, marched on Shu by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made forward general of the northern campaign and, with the western expedition general Tang He, invaded Shu on separate routes.

sentences.zh: 和帥廖永忠等以舟師攻瞿塘，友德帥顧時等以步騎出秦、隴。

translations.literal: He led Liao Yongzhong and others with the fleet to attack Qutang, while Youde led Gu Shi and others with infantry and cavalry out through Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He took Liao Yongzhong and the fleet against Qutang Gorge, while Fu Youde led Gu Shi and the infantry and cavalry through Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 太祖諭友德曰：「蜀人聞我西伐，必悉精銳東守瞿塘，北阻金牛，以抗我師。

translations.literal: Taizu instructed Youde, saying: "When the people of Shu hear that we are attacking from the west, they will surely mass their elite to guard Qutang in the east and block the Golden Ox Road in the north to resist our army.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told Fu Youde: "When the Shu hear we are coming from the west, they will surely mass their best troops to hold Qutang in the east and block the Golden Ox Road in the north against us.

sentences.zh: 若出不意，直搗階、文，門戶既隳，腹心自潰。

translations.literal: If you strike where they do not expect it and drive straight at Jie and Wen, once their gates are broken their heartland will collapse of itself.
translations.idiomatic: If you strike where they do not expect it and drive straight at Jie and Wen, once their gates are smashed their heartland will collapse on its own.

sentences.zh: 兵貴神速，患不勇耳。」

translations.literal: In war speed is precious; the only worry is lack of courage.
translations.idiomatic: In war speed is everything; the only danger is lack of courage.

sentences.zh: 友德疾馳至陝，集諸軍聲言出金牛，而潛引兵趨陳倉，攀援岩穀，晝夜行。

translations.literal: Youde galloped swiftly to Shaan, gathered the armies, and publicly announced that he would march out by the Golden Ox Road, while secretly leading his troops toward Chencang, climbing cliffs and ravines, marching day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youde raced to Shaan, assembled the armies, and announced he would take the Golden Ox Road, while secretly marching on Chencang, scaling cliffs and gorges day and night.

sentences.zh: 抵階州，敗蜀將丁世珍，克其城。

translations.literal: He reached Jiezhou, defeated the Shu general Ding Shizhen, and took its city.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Jiezhou, defeated the Shu general Ding Shizhen, and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 蜀人斷白龍江橋。

translations.literal: The Shu people destroyed the Bailong River bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu destroyed the bridge over the Bailong River.

sentences.zh: 友德修橋以渡，破五里關，遂拔文州。

translations.literal: Youde repaired the bridge to cross, broke through Wuli Pass, and then took Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youde rebuilt the bridge to cross, forced Wuli Pass, and took Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 渡白水江，趨綿州。

translations.literal: He crossed the White Water River and pressed on to Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the White Water River and hurried on to Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時漢江水漲，不得渡，伐木造戰艦。

translations.literal: At that time the Han River was in flood and could not be crossed; he felled trees to build war junks.
translations.idiomatic: The Han River was swollen and impassable, so he felled timber to build warships.

sentences.zh: 欲以軍聲通瞿塘，乃削木為牌為千，書克階、文、綿日月，投漢水，順流下。

translations.literal: Wishing to carry his army's fame to Qutang, he carved a thousand wooden plaques inscribed with the months and days of the capture of Jie, Wen, and Mian, cast them into the Han River, and let them drift downstream.
translations.idiomatic: To carry word of his army to Qutang, he carved a thousand wooden plaques marked with the dates of taking Jie, Wen, and Mian, floated them down the Han, and let the current bear them away.

sentences.zh: 蜀守者見之，皆解體。

translations.literal: The Shu defenders who saw them all lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Shu defenders who saw them lost all fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 初，蜀人聞大軍西征，丞相戴壽等果悉眾守瞿塘。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Shu heard that the great army was marching west, the chancellor Dai Shou and others had indeed massed their entire force to guard Qutang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shu learned the main army was marching west, Chancellor Dai Shou and others had indeed concentrated their full strength at Qutang.

sentences.zh: 及聞友德破階、文，搗江油，始分兵援漢州，以保成都。

translations.literal: When they heard that Youde had taken Jie and Wen and was striking toward Jiangyou, they then divided troops to relieve Hanzhou and protect Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Fu Youde had broken Jie and Wen and was driving on Jiangyou, they split their forces to relieve Hanzhou and shield Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 未至，友德已破其守將向大亨于城下，謂將士曰：「援師遠來，聞大亨破，己膽落，無能為也。」

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Youde had already defeated their defending general Xiang Daheng below the walls and said to his officers and men: "The relief army comes from afar; hearing that Daheng is broken, their courage is already gone and they can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Fu Youde had already beaten their defender Xiang Daheng beneath the walls and told his men: "The relief force comes from far off; once they hear Daheng is broken, their nerve will be gone and they will be helpless.

sentences.zh: 迎擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: He went out to meet them and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He marched out to meet them and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 遂拔漢州，進圍成都。

translations.literal: He then took Hanzhou and advanced to besiege Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Hanzhou and pressed on to besiege Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 壽等以象戰。

translations.literal: Shou and the others fought with war elephants.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shou and his colleagues fought with war elephants.

sentences.zh: 友德令強弩火器沖之，身中流矢不退，將士殊死戰。

translations.literal: Youde ordered powerful crossbows and firearms to charge them; though struck by arrows in the body, he did not withdraw, and officers and men fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youde sent heavy crossbows and firearms against them; though wounded, he would not pull back, and his men fought as if their lives depended on it.

sentences.zh: 象反走，躪藉死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The elephants turned and fled, trampling and killing many.
translations.idiomatic: The elephants turned and stampeded, crushing many of their own side.

sentences.zh: 壽等聞其主明升已降，乃籍府庫倉廩面縛詣軍門。

translations.literal: When Shou and the others heard that their lord Ming Sheng had already surrendered, they inventoried the treasuries and granaries, bound themselves, and came to the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: Learning their lord Ming Sheng had already surrendered, Dai Shou and the others inventoried the treasuries and granaries, bound themselves, and came to the gate of the camp.

sentences.zh: 成都平。

translations.literal: Chengdu was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu was pacified.

sentences.zh: 分兵徇州邑未下者，克保甯，執吳友仁送京師，蜀地悉定。

translations.literal: He divided his forces to subdue prefectures and districts not yet taken, took Baoning, seized Wu Youren and sent him to the capital, and all Shu territory was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He sent columns to bring in holdout prefectures, took Baoning, captured Wu Youren and sent him to the capital, and all Shu was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 友德之攻漢州也，湯和尚頓軍大溪口。

translations.literal: When Youde was attacking Hanzhou, Tang He and the others were still encamped at Daxikou.
translations.idiomatic: While Fu Youde was fighting at Hanzhou, Tang He and his fleet were still halted at Daxikou.

sentences.zh: 既于江流得木牌，乃進師。

translations.literal: Once they found the wooden plaques in the river current, they then advanced their army.
translations.idiomatic: When they found the wooden plaques drifting downriver, they advanced.

sentences.zh: 而戴壽等撤其精兵西救漢州，留老弱守瞿塘，故永忠等得乘勝搗重慶，降明升，於是太祖制《平西蜀文》，盛稱友德功為第一，廖永忠次之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Dai Shou and the others had withdrawn their elite troops west to relieve Hanzhou, leaving only the old and weak to guard Qutang, so Yongzhong and the others were able to exploit the victory to strike Chongqing, receive Ming Sheng's surrender, and thereupon Taizu composed the "Proclamation on Pacifying Western Shu," greatly praising Youde's merit as first and Liao Yongzhong's as second.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shou had meanwhile pulled his best troops west toward Hanzhou, leaving only the old and weak at Qutang, so Yongzhong and the others could press the advantage to Chongqing and accept Ming Sheng's surrender; Taizu then wrote the "Proclamation on Pacifying Western Shu," ranking Fu Youde's merit first and Liao Yongzhong's second.

sentences.zh: 師還，受上賞。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he received the highest rewards.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he received the highest rewards.

sentences.zh: 五年副征西將軍馮勝征沙漠，敗失剌罕於西涼，至永昌，敗太尉朵兒只巴，獲馬牛羊十余萬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served as deputy to the western expedition general Feng Sheng against the desert, defeated Shilahān at Xiliang, reached Yongchang, defeated the grand preceptor Dorjiba, and captured more than a hundred thousand horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he served under the western expedition general Feng Sheng against the steppe, defeated Shilahān at Xiliang, reached Yongchang, routed Grand Preceptor Dorjiba, and took more than a hundred thousand horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 略甘肅，射殺平章不花，降太尉鎖納兒等。

translations.literal: He raided Gansu, shot and killed the minister Buluqan, and received the surrender of Grand Preceptor Suonai'er and others.
translations.idiomatic: He raided Gansu, killed the minister Buluqan with an arrow, and accepted the surrender of Grand Preceptor Suonai'er and others.

sentences.zh: 至瓜沙州，獲金銀印及雜畜二萬而還。

translations.literal: Reaching Guazhou and Shazhou, he obtained gold and silver seals and more than twenty thousand miscellaneous livestock and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Guazhou and Shazhou he seized gold and silver seals and more than twenty thousand head of livestock before returning.

sentences.zh: 是時師出三道，獨友德全勝。

translations.literal: At that time the army went out on three routes, and Youde alone won complete victory.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign sent three columns; only Fu Youde returned victorious throughout.

sentences.zh: 以主將勝坐小法，賞不行。

translations.literal: Because the commander-in-chief Sheng was punished under a minor statute, rewards were not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Because the commander Feng Sheng was penalized for a minor infraction, the rewards were never granted.

sentences.zh: 明年復出雁門，為前鋒，獲平章鄧孛羅帖木兒。

translations.literal: The next year he again went out through Yanmen as vanguard and captured the minister Deng Boluotiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he marched out through Yanmen as vanguard and captured the minister Deng Boluotiemuer.

sentences.zh: 還鎮北平，陳便宜五事。

translations.literal: On his return he garrisoned Beiping and submitted five proposals of practical benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he garrisoned Beiping and submitted five practical proposals.

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 召還，從太子講武于荊山，益歲祿千石。

translations.literal: He was recalled and followed the crown prince in military exercises at Jingshan; his annual emolument was increased by a thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he joined the crown prince in war games at Jingshan, and his annual stipend was raised by a thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 九年破擒伯顏帖木兒于延安，降其眾。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he defeated and captured Boyantiemuer at Yan'an and received the surrender of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he defeated and captured Boyantiemuer at Yan'an and accepted the surrender of his followers.

sentences.zh: 帝將征雲南，命友德巡行川、蜀、雅、播之境，修城郭，繕關梁，因兵威降金築、普定諸山寨。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to campaign against Yunnan; he ordered Youde to tour the territories of Chuan, Shu, Ya, and Bo, repair city walls, restore passes and bridges, and by military might bring the stockaded villages of Jinzhu, Puding, and others to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prepared to conquer Yunnan, he sent Youde to survey Sichuan and the Ya and Bo borderlands, repair fortifications and crossings, and use the army's prestige to win over the Jinzhu and Puding hill forts.

sentences.zh: 十四年副大將軍達出塞，討乃兒不花，渡北黃河，襲灰山，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he served as deputy to the great general Da on an expedition beyond the passes against Nayirbuhua, crossed the Northern Yellow River, raided Huishan, and killed and captured in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he marched as Xu Da's deputy beyond the frontier against Nayirbuhua, crossed the northern Yellow River, struck Huishan, and took a great toll in enemy dead and captives.

sentences.zh: 其年秋充征南將軍，帥左副將軍藍玉、右副將軍沐英，將步騎三十萬征雲南。

translations.literal: That autumn he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South, leading the left deputy general Lan Yu and the right deputy general Mu Ying with three hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to campaign against Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he became General Who Pacifies the South, with Lan Yu as his left deputy and Mu Ying as his right, and led three hundred thousand foot and horse south against Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 至湖廣，分遣都督胡海等將兵五萬由永甯趨烏撒，而自帥大軍由辰、沅趨貴州。

translations.literal: Reaching Huguang, he separately sent the commander Hu Hai and others with fifty thousand troops from Yongning toward Wusa, while he himself led the main army from Chen and Yuan toward Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Huguang he detached Commander Hu Hai with fifty thousand men to advance from Yongning on Wusa, while he took the main force by way of Chen and Yuan into Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 克普定、普安，降諸苗蠻。

translations.literal: He took Puding and Pu'an and received the submission of the various Miao tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Puding and Pu'an and brought the Miao clans to submit.

sentences.zh: 進攻曲靖，大戰白石江，擒元平章達裏麻。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Qujing, he fought a great battle on the Baishi River and captured the Yuan prefectural minister Dalima.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on to Qujing, he fought a major battle on the Baishi River and took the Yuan minister Dalima prisoner.

sentences.zh: 遂擊烏撒，循格孤山而南，以通永寧之兵，遣兩將軍趨雲南。

translations.literal: He then struck Wusa, followed Gegu Mountain southward to link with Yongning's troops, and sent the two deputy generals to press toward Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Wusa, marched south along Gegu Mountain to join Yongning's column, and dispatched both deputies toward Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 元梁王走死。

translations.literal: The Yuan Prince of Liang fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan Prince of Liang fled to his death.

sentences.zh: 友德城烏撒，群蠻來爭，奮擊破之，得七星關以通畢節。

translations.literal: Youde fortified Wusa; the tribes came to contest it; he fought fiercely and defeated them, seizing Qixing Pass to open the route to Bijie.
translations.idiomatic: Youde walled Wusa; when the tribes massed to take it back, he drove them off and seized Qixing Pass, opening the road to Bijie.

sentences.zh: 又克可渡河，降東川、烏蒙、芒部諸蠻。

translations.literal: He also took the Ke River crossing and received the submission of the tribes of Dongchuan, Wumeng, and Mangbu.
translations.idiomatic: He next secured the Ke River ford and won over the Dongchuan, Wumeng, and Mangbu tribes.

sentences.zh: 烏撒諸蠻復叛，討之，斬首三萬餘級，獲牛馬十余萬，水西諸部皆降。

translations.literal: The tribes of Wusa rebelled again; he campaigned against them, beheaded more than thirty thousand, seized over a hundred thousand cattle and horses, and all the Shui Xi departments submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wusa tribes rose again, he suppressed them, taking more than thirty thousand heads and over a hundred thousand cattle and horses; every Shui Xi department then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十七年論功進封潁國公，食祿三千石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, for merit he was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of Ying, with an emolument of three thousand piculs and a hereditary patent granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 his deeds won him promotion to Duke of Ying, with a stipend of three thousand piculs and a patent of hereditary entitlement.

sentences.zh: 十九年帥師討平雲南蠻。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he led troops to campaign and pacify the Yunnan tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he led an army that pacified the Yunnan tribes.

sentences.zh: 二十年副大將軍馮勝，征納哈出於金山。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he served as deputy to the great general Feng Sheng in campaigning against Nahaeru at Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he was Feng Sheng's deputy in the expedition against Nahaeru at Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，東川蠻叛，復為征南將軍，帥師討平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Dongchuan tribes rebelled; he was again made General Who Pacifies the South and led troops to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21, when the Dongchuan tribes rebelled, he was again named General Who Pacifies the South and led a force that subdued them.

sentences.zh: 移兵討越州叛酋阿資，明年破之于普安。

translations.literal: He shifted troops to campaign against the rebel chieftain Azi of Yuezhou; the following year he defeated him at Pu'an.
translations.idiomatic: He turned his army on the Yuezhou rebel Azi and broke him at Pu'an the next year.

sentences.zh: 二十三年從晉王、燕王征沙漠，擒乃兒不花，還駐開平，復征寧夏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he followed the Prince of Jin and the Prince of Yan in campaigning in the desert, captured Nayirbuhua, returned to garrison at Kaiping, and again campaigned in Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he marched with the princes of Jin and Yan into the desert, captured Nayirbuhua, returned to hold Kaiping, and campaigned again in Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 明年為征虜將軍，備邊北平。

translations.literal: The following year he was made General Who Subdues the Barbarians and prepared the border defenses of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became General Who Subdues the Barbarians and stood guard on the Beiping frontier.

sentences.zh: 復從燕王征哈者舍利，追元遼王。

translations.literal: Again he followed the Prince of Yan in campaigning against Hajizhali and pursued the Yuan Prince of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the Prince of Yan against Hajizhali and pursued the Yuan Prince of Liao.

sentences.zh: 軍甫行，遽令班師。

translations.literal: The army had just set out when he was abruptly ordered to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The columns had scarcely marched when he was suddenly ordered home.

sentences.zh: 敵不設備，因潛師深入至黑嶺，大破敵眾而還。

translations.literal: The enemy were unprepared; he therefore sent troops secretly deep inland to Heiling, routed the enemy host greatly, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy were off guard; he slipped a detachment deep inland to Heiling, routed them in force, and came back.

sentences.zh: 再出，練兵山、陝，總屯田事。

translations.literal: He went out again, drilled troops in the mountains of Shaanxi, and oversaw all garrison-farming affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On another deployment he trained troops in the Shaanxi hills and superintended military colonization.

sentences.zh: 加太子太師，尋遣還鄉。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and soon after was sent back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Tutor of the crown prince and soon afterward sent home.

sentences.zh: 友德喑啞跳蕩，身冒百死。

translations.literal: Youde was taciturn and restless, personally risking death a hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: Youde was sparing of speech but fierce in action, exposing himself to mortal danger again and again.

sentences.zh: 自偏裨至大將，每戰必先士卒。

translations.literal: From junior officer to great general, in every battle he was ahead of the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: From company officer to field marshal, he always fought in the front rank.

sentences.zh: 雖被創，戰益力，以故所至立功，帝屢敕獎勞。

translations.literal: Though wounded, he fought all the harder; for this reason wherever he went he achieved merit, and the Emperor repeatedly issued edicts of reward and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded, he only fought harder; everywhere he marched he won glory, and the emperor repeatedly sent edicts of praise and reward.

sentences.zh: 子忠，尚壽春公主，女為晉世子濟熺妃。

translations.literal: His son Zhong married the Princess of Shouchun; his daughter became consort to Jili, heir of the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong wed the Princess of Shouchun; his daughter married Jili, heir to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 廖永忠

translations.literal: Liao Yongzhong
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yongzhong

sentences.zh: 廖永忠，巢人，楚國公永安弟也。

translations.literal: Liao Yongzhong, a man of Chao, was the younger brother of Yong'an, Duke of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yongzhong, a native of Chao, was the younger brother of Yong'an, Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 從永安迎太祖于巢湖，年最少。

translations.literal: He followed Yong'an to welcome the Founding Emperor at Chaohu; he was the youngest.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Yong'an to meet the founding emperor at Chaohu and was the youngest in the party.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「汝亦欲富貴乎？」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said: "Do you too desire wealth and rank?"
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor asked, "Do you also want wealth and honor?"

sentences.zh: 永忠曰：「獲事明主，掃除寇亂，垂名竹帛，是所願耳。」

translations.literal: Yongzhong said: "To serve an enlightened lord, sweep away rebels and disorder, and leave one's name on silk and bamboo—that is my desire."
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong replied, "To serve a wise sovereign, clear away banditry and chaos, and win a name that endures in the histories—that is all I wish."

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉焉。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 副永安將水軍渡江，拔採石、太平，擒陳野先，破蠻子海牙及陳兆先，定集慶，克鎮江、常州、池州，討江陰海寇，皆有功。

translations.literal: As deputy to Yong'an he led the navy across the river, took Caishi and Taiping, captured Chen Yexian, defeated Manzi Haiya and Chen Zhaoxian, secured Jiqing, and took Zhenjiang, Changzhou, and Chizhou; campaigning against the sea bandits of Jiangyin, he achieved merit in every action.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Yong'an, he commanded the fleet across the Yangtze, seized Caishi and Taiping, took Chen Yexian, broke Manzi Haiya and Chen Zhaoxian, secured the capital region, captured Zhenjiang, Changzhou, and Chizhou, and routed the Jiangyin pirates—earning credit at every turn.

sentences.zh: 永安陷於吳，以永忠襲兄職，為樞密僉院，總其軍。

translations.literal: When Yong'an was trapped by Wu, Yongzhong inherited his brother's post as Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and took command of his army.
translations.idiomatic: After Yong'an fell into Wu hands, Yongzhong succeeded to his brother's post as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and assumed command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 攻趙普勝柵江營，復池州。

translations.literal: He attacked Zhao Pusheng's stockade at Jiangying and recovered Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Zhao Pusheng's camp at Jiangying and retook Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒犯龍江，大呼突陣，諸軍從其後，大敗之。

translations.literal: When Chen Youliang attacked Longjiang, he shouted and charged the enemy line; the armies followed from behind and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang struck Longjiang, he charged the enemy ranks with a battle cry; the troops followed and put them to rout.

sentences.zh: 從伐友諒，至安慶，破其水寨，遂克安慶。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Youliang, he reached Anqing, broke its naval stockade, and then took Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Youliang he reached Anqing, destroyed its river fort, and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 從攻江州，州城臨江，守備甚固。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Jiangzhou, the city stood on the river and its defenses were very strong.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Jiangzhou, the city lay on the river and was heavily fortified.

sentences.zh: 永忠度城高下，造橋於船尾，名曰天橋，以船乘風倒行，橋傅於城，遂克之。

translations.literal: Yongzhong gauged the height of the walls, built a bridge on the sterns of boats called the Sky Bridge, had the boats sail backward with the wind, fixed the bridge to the wall, and thus took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong measured the wall height, rigged a "Sky Bridge" from the sterns of his ships, ran the fleet backward before the wind until the bridge caught the battlements, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 進中書省右丞。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從下南昌，援安豐，戰鄱陽湖，決圍殊死戰。

translations.literal: He followed in the reduction of Nanchang, relieved Anfeng, fought at Poyang Lake, and broke the encirclement in desperate combat.
translations.idiomatic: He helped reduce Nanchang, relieved Anfeng, fought at Poyang Lake, and broke through the siege in a desperate battle.

sentences.zh: 敵將張定邊直犯太祖舟，常遇春射走之。

translations.literal: The enemy general Zhang Dingbian charged straight at the Founding Emperor's boat; Chang Yuchun shot and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy commander Zhang Dingbian bore straight for the founding emperor's flagship; Chang Yuchun shot him back.

sentences.zh: 永忠乘飛舸追且射，定邊被百餘矢，漢卒多死傷。

translations.literal: Yongzhong took a swift boat in pursuit and shot; Dingbian was struck by more than a hundred arrows, and many Han soldiers were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong gave chase in a fast galley, riddling Dingbian with more than a hundred arrows and leaving many of the Han troops dead or wounded.

sentences.zh: 明日，復與俞通海等以七舟載葦荻，乘風縱火，焚敵樓船數百。

translations.literal: The next day, together with Yu Tonghai and others, he loaded seven boats with reeds, rode the wind to set fires, and burned several hundred of the enemy's tower ships.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he and Yu Tonghai and others packed seven boats with reeds, ran before the wind, and burned hundreds of enemy tower ships.

sentences.zh: 又以六舟深入搏戰，復旋繞而出，敵驚為神。

translations.literal: Again with six boats he fought deep in the enemy line, then wheeled and came out; the enemy took him for a god.
translations.idiomatic: With six more boats he plunged into the thick of the fight, wheeled about, and broke clear again—the enemy thought him supernatural.

sentences.zh: 又邀擊之涇江口，友諒死。

translations.literal: He also intercepted them at the mouth of the Jing River; Youliang died.
translations.idiomatic: He intercepted them again at the mouth of the Jing River, where Youliang was killed.

sentences.zh: 從征陳理，分兵柵四門，于江中連舟為長寨，絕其出入，理降。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Chen Li, he divided troops to block the four gates, linked boats in the river into a long stockade to cut off exit and entry, and Li surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Chen Li he blocked all four gates and chained boats on the river into a long barricade that sealed the city; Li surrendered.

sentences.zh: 還京，太祖以漆牌書「功超群將，智邁雄師」八字賜之，懸於門。
