translations.literal: Returning to the capital, the Founding Emperor bestowed on him a lacquered plaque inscribed with eight characters: "Merit surpasses the host of generals; wisdom transcends the heroic host," and had it hung at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, the founding emperor gave him a lacquered plaque bearing eight characters—"Merit surpasses every general; wisdom outstrips the boldest host"—and ordered it hung above his gate.

sentences.zh: 已，從徐達取淮東，張士誠遣舟師薄海安，太祖令永忠還兵水寨禦之，達遂克淮東諸郡。

translations.literal: Thereafter, following Xu Da in taking eastern Huai, when Zhang Shicheng sent a fleet to press Haian, the Founding Emperor ordered Yongzhong to return to the naval stockade to resist them, and Da then took the eastern Huai commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Later, marching with Xu Da into eastern Huai, he was sent back to the river camp when Zhang Shicheng's fleet threatened Haian; Xu Da then secured the eastern Huai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 從伐士誠，取德清，進克平江，拜中書平章政事。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Shicheng, he took Deqing, advanced to capture Pingjiang, and was appointed Grand Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the war on Shicheng he seized Deqing, pressed on to take Pingjiang, and was made grand director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋充征南副將軍，帥舟師自海道會湯和，討降方國珍，進克福州。

translations.literal: Soon he was made deputy general who pacifies the south, leading the fleet by sea to join Tang He in campaigning to reduce Fang Guozhen, and advanced to take Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named deputy general who pacifies the south, led the fleet by sea to join Tang He against Fang Guozhen, and advanced to capture Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年兼同知詹事院事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he also served as associate director of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 1 he also served as associate director of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 略定閩中諸郡，至延平，破執陳友定。

translations.literal: He pacified the commanderies of Fujian, reaching Yanping, where he defeated and captured Chen Youding.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the Fujian commanderies, reached Yanping, and defeated and captured Chen Youding.

sentences.zh: 尋拜征南將軍，以硃亮祖為副，由海道取廣東。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South, with Zhu Liangzu as deputy, to take Guangdong by sea.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General Who Pacifies the South, with Zhu Liangzu as his deputy, to seize Guangdong by sea.

sentences.zh: 永忠先發書諭元左丞何真，曉譬利害。

translations.literal: Yongzhong first sent a letter instructing the Yuan left minister He Zhen, explaining advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong first wrote to the Yuan left minister He Zhen, setting out the costs and benefits of resistance.

sentences.zh: 真即奉表請降。

translations.literal: Zhen at once submitted a memorial requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen promptly sent in a memorial offering surrender.

sentences.zh: 至東莞，真帥官屬出迎。

translations.literal: Reaching Dongguan, Zhen led his officials out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongguan, Zhen came out with his officials to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 至廣州，降盧左丞。

translations.literal: Reaching Guangzhou, he received the surrender of the Yuan left minister Lu.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangzhou he accepted the surrender of the Yuan left minister Lu.

sentences.zh: 擒海寇邵宗愚，數其殘暴斬之。

translations.literal: He captured the sea bandit Shao Zongyu, enumerated his atrocities, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the pirate Shao Zongyu, denounced his crimes, and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 廣人大悅。

translations.literal: The people of Guang were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangdong rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 馳諭九真、日南、硃崖、儋耳三十餘城，皆納印請吏。

translations.literal: He sent riders to announce to more than thirty cities of Jiuzhen, Rinan, Zhuya, and Dan'er; all surrendered their seals and requested officials.
translations.idiomatic: He sent messengers to more than thirty cities as far as Jiuzhen, Rinan, Zhuya, and Dan'er; all surrendered their seals and asked for imperial magistrates.

sentences.zh: 進取廣西，至梧州，降元達魯花赤拜住，潯、柳諸路皆下。

translations.literal: Advancing to take Guangxi, he reached Wuzhou, received the surrender of the Yuan darughachi Baizhu, and the routes of Xun and Liu all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Moving into Guangxi, he reached Wuzhou, accepted the surrender of the Yuan darughachi Baizhu, and the Xun and Liu circuits submitted.

sentences.zh: 遣亮祖會楊璟收未下州郡。

translations.literal: He sent Liangzu to join Yang Jing in receiving the commanderies not yet taken.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liangzu to join Yang Jing in reducing the remaining prefectures.

sentences.zh: 永忠引兵克南寧，降象州。

translations.literal: Yongzhong led troops to take Nanning and received the surrender of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong himself took Nanning and accepted the surrender of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 兩廣悉平。

translations.literal: The two Guang were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Both Guang provinces were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 永忠善撫綏，民懷其惠，為之立祠。

translations.literal: Yongzhong was skilled at soothing and comforting; the people cherished his kindness and built temples for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong governed with a gentle hand; the people loved him for it and raised temples in his honor.

sentences.zh: 明年九月還京師，帝命太子帥百官迎勞于龍江。

translations.literal: The following year, in the ninth month, he returned to the capital; the Emperor ordered the crown prince to lead the hundred officials in welcoming and consoling him at Longjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the ninth month, he returned to the capital; the emperor had the crown prince and the full court welcome him at Longjiang.

sentences.zh: 入見，仍命太子送還第。

translations.literal: On entering audience he was again ordered to have the crown prince escort him back to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: After his audience the crown prince was again sent to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 復出，撫定泉、漳。

translations.literal: He went out again to soothe and settle Quan and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out once more to pacify Quanzhou and Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年從大將軍徐達北征，克察罕腦兒。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the great general Xu Da on the northern expedition and took Chahan'nao'er.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he joined the great general Xu Da on the northern campaign and captured Chahan'nao'er.

sentences.zh: 還，封德慶侯，食祿一千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: On returning he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Deqing, with an emolument of one thousand five hundred piculs and a hereditary patent granted.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Marquis of Deqing, with a stipend of fifteen hundred piculs and a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 明年，以征西副將軍從湯和帥舟師伐蜀。

translations.literal: The following year, as deputy general of the western expedition, he followed Tang He in leading the fleet to campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as deputy commander of the western expedition, he followed Tang He's fleet against Shu.

sentences.zh: 和駐大溪口，永忠先發。

translations.literal: Tang He halted at Daxikou; Yongzhong advanced first.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He halted at Daxikou; Yongzhong went on ahead.

sentences.zh: 及舊夔府，破守將鄒興等兵。

translations.literal: Reaching the old Kui Prefecture, he defeated the defending troops of Zou Xing and others.
translations.idiomatic: At old Kui Prefecture he broke the garrison of Zou Xing and others.

sentences.zh: 進至瞿塘關，山峻水急，蜀人設鐵鎖橋，橫據關口，舟不得進。

translations.literal: Advancing to Qutang Pass, the mountains were steep and the waters swift; the Shu people set an iron-chain bridge spanning the pass so that boats could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: At Qutang Pass the cliffs were sheer and the current fierce; the Shu defenders had spanned the narrows with an iron-chain bridge that blocked the fleet.

sentences.zh: 永忠密遣數百人持糗糧水筒，舁小舟逾山渡關，出其上流。

translations.literal: Yongzhong secretly sent several hundred men carrying dry rations in water tubes, shouldering small boats over the mountains to cross the pass and emerge above it on the upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong secretly sent several hundred men with dry rations in bamboo tubes, carrying light boats over the mountains to cross above the pass.

sentences.zh: 蜀山多草木，令將士皆衣青蓑衣，魚貫走崖石間。

translations.literal: The Shu mountains had much grass and wood; he ordered the soldiers all to wear green rain capes and to file in single line along the cliff rocks.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan hills were thick with brush; he had his men cloak themselves in green straw rain capes and snake single file along the cliffs.

sentences.zh: 度已至，帥精銳出墨葉渡，夜五鼓，分兩軍攻其水陸寨。

translations.literal: When they had arrived, he led picked troops out at Moyed Crossing; at the fifth watch of the night he divided into two armies and attacked their water and land stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Once they were in place, he led elite troops out at Moyed Crossing; at the fifth watch he split into two columns and struck their river and shore camps.

sentences.zh: 水軍皆以鐵裹船頭，置火器而前。

translations.literal: The naval troops all had iron wrapped on the prows of the boats and advanced with fire weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The river force wrapped iron around every prow and advanced with fire weapons.

sentences.zh: 黎明，蜀人始覺，盡銳來拒。

translations.literal: At dawn the Shu people first realized it; they brought out their full strength to resist.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Shu defenders realized what had happened and threw their full strength into the fight.

sentences.zh: 永忠已破其陸寨，會將士舁舟出江者，一時併發，上下夾攻，大破之，鄒興死。

translations.literal: Yongzhong had already broken their land stockade; when the soldiers who carried boats out to the river joined him, they attacked together from above and below, routed them greatly, and Zou Xing died.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong had already overrun the shore camp; when the men who had hauled boats down to the river joined him, the assault from land and water shattered the enemy and Zou Xing was killed.

sentences.zh: 遂焚三橋，斷橫江鐵索，擒同僉蔣達等八十餘人。

translations.literal: He then burned the three bridges, severed the iron chains across the river, and captured more than eighty men including the associate minister Jiang Da.
translations.idiomatic: He burned the three bridges, cut the iron chains across the Yangtze, and took more than eighty prisoners, including the associate minister Jiang Da.

sentences.zh: 飛天張、鐵頭張等皆遁去，遂入夔府。

translations.literal: Feitian Zhang, Tietou Zhang, and others all fled; he then entered Kui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feitian Zhang, Tietou Zhang, and others fled; he entered Kui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明日，和始至，乃與和分道進，期會于重慶。

translations.literal: The next day He arrived; then he and He advanced by separate routes, agreeing to meet at Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He arrived the next day; the two commanders then advanced by separate routes, planning to rendezvous at Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 永忠帥舟師直搗重慶，次銅鑼峽。

translations.literal: Yongzhong led the fleet straight to Chongqing and anchored at Tongluo Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong drove the fleet straight for Chongqing and moored at Tongluo Gorge.

sentences.zh: 蜀主明升請降，永忠以和未至辭。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler Ming Sheng requested surrender; Yongzhong declined because He had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler Ming Sheng offered to surrender, but Yongzhong refused until He arrived.

sentences.zh: 俟和至，乃受降，承制撫慰。

translations.literal: When He arrived, he then accepted the surrender and, by imperial commission, comforted and reassured them.
translations.idiomatic: Once He came up, he accepted the surrender and, acting on imperial authority, reassured the population.

sentences.zh: 下令禁侵掠。

translations.literal: He issued orders forbidding looting.
translations.idiomatic: He issued strict orders against pillage.

sentences.zh: 卒取民七茄，立斬之。

translations.literal: A soldier took seven eggplants from the people; he had him beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: When a soldier stole seven eggplants from a household, he had him executed at once.

sentences.zh: 慰安戴壽、向大享等家，令其子弟持書往成都招諭。

translations.literal: He comforted the families of Dai Shou, Xiang Daxiang, and others, and had their sons and younger brothers carry letters to Chengdu to summon them to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He sent condolences to the families of Dai Shou and Xiang Daxiang and had their sons carry letters to Chengdu urging surrender.

sentences.zh: 壽等已為傅友德所敗，及得書，遂降。

translations.literal: Shou and the others had already been defeated by Fu Youde; on receiving the letters, they then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shou and the others had already been beaten by Fu Youde; the letters brought them in.

sentences.zh: 蜀地悉平。

translations.literal: The Shu territory was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: All of Shu was pacified.

sentences.zh: 帝制《平蜀文》旌其功，有「傅一廖二」之語，褒賚甚厚。

translations.literal: The Emperor composed the "Text on the Pacification of Shu" to proclaim his merit, with the phrase "Fu first, Liao second," and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote the "Text on the Pacification of Shu" to honor his achievement, praising "Fu first, Liao second," and heaped rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 明年北征，至和林。

translations.literal: The following year on the northern expedition he reached Helin.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on the northern campaign, he reached Helin.

sentences.zh: 六年督舟師出海捕倭，尋還京。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he supervised the fleet in putting to sea to hunt Wo pirates, and soon returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he commanded the fleet at sea against Japanese pirates, then returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，韓林兒在滁州，太祖遣永忠迎歸應天，至瓜步覆其舟死，帝以咎永忠。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Han Lin'er was at Chuzhou, the Founding Emperor sent Yongzhong to welcome him back to Yingtian; reaching Guabu, he capsized the boat and Lin'er drowned; the Emperor blamed Yongzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Han Lin'er was at Chuzhou, the founding emperor sent Yongzhong to bring him to Yingtian; at Guabu the boat was swamped and Lin'er drowned—the emperor held Yongzhong responsible.

sentences.zh: 及大封功臣，諭諸將曰：「永忠戰鄱陽時，忘軀拒敵，可謂奇男子。

translations.literal: When the great enfeoffment of meritorious ministers took place, he instructed the generals, saying: "At Poyang, Yongzhong forgot his body and repelled the enemy; he may be called a singular man.
translations.idiomatic: At the great enfeoffment of his generals, the emperor told them, "At Poyang, Yongzhong risked his life against the enemy—a singular man.

sentences.zh: 然使所善儒生窺朕意，徼封爵，故止封侯而不公。」

translations.literal: Yet he had a Confucian scholar he favored spy out my intent and seek a noble enfeoffment; therefore I stopped at making him a marquis and did not make him a duke."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he let a scholar he favored read my mind and angle for a dukedom, so I made him only a marquis and not a duke."

sentences.zh: 及楊憲為相，永忠與相比。

translations.literal: When Yang Xian became chancellor, Yongzhong became his ally.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yang Xian became chief minister, Yongzhong aligned with him.

sentences.zh: 憲誅，永忠以功大得免。

translations.literal: When Xian was executed, Yongzhong was spared because his merits were great.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xian was executed, Yongzhong was spared on account of his great services.

sentences.zh: 八年三月坐僭用龍鳳諸不法事，賜死，年五十三。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year he was charged with unlawfully using dragon-and-phoenix regalia and other illegal acts, granted death, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year (1375) he was condemned for presumptuous use of dragon-and-phoenix insignia and other unlawful acts, and was granted death; he was fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 子權，十三年嗣侯，從傅友德征雲南，守畢節及瀘州，召還。

translations.literal: His son Quan in the thirteenth year inherited the marquisate, followed Fu Youde on the Yunnan campaign, garrisoned Bijie and Luzhou, and was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan inherited the marquisate in the thirteenth year, followed Fu Youde against Yunnan, held Bijie and Luzhou, and was recalled.

sentences.zh: 十七年卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year.

sentences.zh: 子鏞不得嗣，以嫡子為散騎舍人，累官都督。

translations.literal: His son Yong could not inherit; as legitimate son he became a Gentleman Attendant of the Casual Cavalry and rose through offices to Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong could not succeed to the title; as the legitimate heir he served as Gentleman Attendant of the Casual Cavalry and rose to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 建文時與議兵事，宿衛殿廷。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign he participated in military deliberations and served as palace guard in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jianwen emperor he took part in military councils and stood guard in the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 與弟銘皆嘗受學于方孝孺。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Ming had both studied under Fang Xiaoru.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Ming had both been pupils of Fang Xiaoru.

sentences.zh: 孝孺死，鏞、銘收其遺骸，葬到處寶門外山上。

translations.literal: When Xiaoru died, Yong and Ming recovered his remains and buried them on the hill outside Jubao Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaoru was killed, Yong and Ming gathered his remains and buried them on the hill outside Jubao Gate.

sentences.zh: 甫畢，亦見收，論死。

translations.literal: As soon as they had finished, they too were arrested and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had they finished when they too were seized and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 弟鉞及從父指揮僉事升俱戍邊。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yue and his uncle by the paternal line, the Assistant Commander Sheng, were both sent to garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yue and his paternal uncle, Assistant Commander Sheng, were both banished to border service.

sentences.zh: 初，廖永忠等之歸太祖也，趙庸兄弟亦俱降，後亦有過不得封公，與永忠類。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Liao Yongzhong and others submitted to the Taizu, the Zhao Yong brothers also surrendered together; later they too had faults and could not be enfeoffed as dukes, similar to Yongzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liao Yongzhong and others came over to the Taizu, the Zhao Yong brothers surrendered as well; they too later had faults that kept them from a ducal enfeoffment, much like Yongzhong.

sentences.zh: 庸，廬州人，與兄仲中聚眾結水寨，屯巢湖，歸太祖。

translations.literal: Yong was a man of Luzhou; with his elder brother Zhongzhong he gathered a crowd, formed a water stockade, encamped at Chaohu Lake, and submitted to the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was a native of Luzhou; he and his elder brother Zhongzhong raised men, built a water stockade on Chaohu Lake, and submitted to the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 仲中累功為行樞密院僉事，守安慶。

translations.literal: Zhongzhong through accumulated merit became Commissioner of the Branch Secretariat for Military Affairs and guarded Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhong rose by repeated merit to Commissioner of the Branch Secretariat for Military Affairs and held Anqing.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒陷安慶，仲中棄城走還龍江，法當誅。

translations.literal: When Chen Youliang took Anqing, Zhongzhong abandoned the city and fled back to Longjiang; by law he should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang seized Anqing, Zhongzhong abandoned the city and fled to Longjiang; the law called for his execution.

sentences.zh: 常遇春請原之。

translations.literal: Chang Yuchun asked that he be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun pleaded for his life.

sentences.zh: 太祖不許，曰：「法不行，無以懲後。」

translations.literal: The Taizu did not agree, saying: "If the law is not enforced, there is no way to warn those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu refused, saying, "If the law is not carried out, there is nothing to restrain those who follow.

sentences.zh: 遂誅仲中，而以其官授庸。

translations.literal: He then executed Zhongzhong and gave his office to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Zhongzhong and transferred his post to Yong.

sentences.zh: 從復安慶，徇江西諸路，進參知政事。

translations.literal: He followed in the recovery of Anqing, pacified the circuits of Jiangxi, and was promoted to Vice Administrator of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in retaking Anqing, swept the Jiangxi circuits, and was promoted to Vice Administrator of the Right.

sentences.zh: 從戰康郎山，與俞通海、廖永忠等以六舟深入敗敵。

translations.literal: At the battle of Kanglang Mountain, with Yu Tonghai, Liao Yongzhong, and others he took six boats deep in and defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At Kanglang Mountain he joined Yu Tonghai, Liao Yongzhong, and others in taking six boats deep into the enemy line and routing them.

sentences.zh: 平武昌，克廬州，援安豐，皆有功。

translations.literal: In pacifying Wuchang, taking Luzhou, and relieving Anfeng, he had merit in each.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the pacification of Wuchang, the capture of Luzhou, and the relief of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 大軍取淮東，庸與華高帥舟師克海安、泰州，進國平江。

translations.literal: When the main army took Huaidong, Yong and Hua Gao led the fleet to take Hai'an and Taizhou and advanced to invest Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force secured Huaidong, Yong and Hua Gao led the fleet to take Hai'an and Taizhou and pressed on to besiege Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 吳平，擢中書左丞。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was subdued he was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍取山東。

translations.literal: He followed the Grand General in taking Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Grand General in the conquest of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年命兼太子副詹事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he was ordered to serve concurrently as Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 1 he was appointed concurrently Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 河南平，命庸留守。

translations.literal: When Henan was pacified, Yong was ordered to remain and guard it.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan was pacified, Yong was left to hold it.

sentences.zh: 復分兵渡河，徇下河北州縣，進克河間，守之。

translations.literal: Again he divided troops, crossed the river, pacified the prefectures and counties of Hebei below, advanced to take Hejian, and garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: He again split his force, crossed the river, reduced the Hebei prefectures and counties downstream, took Hejian, and garrisoned it.

sentences.zh: 尋移守保定，並收未復山寨。

translations.literal: Soon he moved to garrison Baoding and also recovered mountain stockades not yet retaken.
translations.idiomatic: He soon shifted to Baoding and also brought in mountain strongholds still unsubdued.

sentences.zh: 又從大軍克太原，下關。

translations.literal: Again he followed the main army in taking Taiyuan and reducing the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He again marched with the main army to take Taiyuan and reduce the passes.

sentences.zh: 陝。

translations.literal: Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi followed.

sentences.zh: 從常遇春北追元帝。

translations.literal: He followed Chang Yuchun north in pursuit of the Yuan emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chang Yuchun in the northern pursuit of the Yuan emperor.

sentences.zh: 師還，遇春卒，命庸為副將軍，同李文忠攻慶陽。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Yuchun died; Yong was appointed deputy general and together with Li Wenzhong attacked Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return Yuchun died; Yong was made deputy general and, with Li Wenzhong, attacked Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 行至太原，元兵攻大同急，文忠與庸謀，以便宜援大同，再敗元兵于馬邑，擒其將脫列伯。

translations.literal: When they reached Taiyuan, Yuan troops were pressing Datong urgently; Wenzhong and Yong deliberated and, using discretionary authority, relieved Datong; they again defeated Yuan troops at Mayi and captured the general Tuoleibo.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan they learned that Yuan forces were pressing Datong hard; Wenzhong and Yong agreed on their own authority to relieve Datong, routed the Yuan again at Mayi, and captured the general Tuoleibo.

sentences.zh: 論功，賞賚亞于大將軍。

translations.literal: In assessing merit, his rewards were second only to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were reckoned, his rewards ranked just below the Grand General's.

sentences.zh: 三年復從文忠北伐，出野狐嶺，克應昌。

translations.literal: In the third year he again followed Wenzhong on the northern campaign, went out through Ye'erzhu, and took Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he again followed Wenzhong north, marched out through Wild Fox Ridge, and took Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 師還，論功最，以在應昌私納奴婢，不得封公，封南雄侯，食祿一千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: When the army returned, his merit was ranked highest; because at Yingchang he had privately taken female slaves and servants, he could not be enfeoffed as a duke; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanxiong with a salary of 1,500 shi and granted an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return his merit was judged foremost, but because he had privately taken bondwomen at Yingchang he could not be made a duke; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Nanxiong at 1,500 shi and given a hereditary iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 已，從伐蜀，中途還。

translations.literal: Thereafter he followed the campaign against Shu but returned midway.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the Shu campaign but turned back before it ended.

sentences.zh: 十四年，閩、粵盜起，命庸討之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, bandits rose in Fujian and Guangdong; Yong was ordered to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year banditry broke out in Fujian and Guangdong, and Yong was sent to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 逾年悉平諸盜及陽山、歸善叛蠻，戮其魁，散遣餘眾，民得復業。

translations.literal: After more than a year he pacified all the bandits and the rebel barbarians of Yangshan and Guishan, executed their chiefs, dispersed the remainder, and the people were able to return to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he had pacified the bandits and the rebel tribes of Yangshan and Guishan, executed their leaders, dispersed the rest, and the people returned to their fields.

sentences.zh: 奏籍蜒戶萬人為水軍。

translations.literal: He memorialized to register ten thousand boat-dwelling households as naval troops.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to enroll ten thousand Tanka households as naval troops.

sentences.zh: 又平廣東盜號鏟平王者，獲賊党萬七千八百餘人，斬首八千八百餘級，降其民萬三千餘戶。

translations.literal: He also pacified Guangdong bandits styled the "King Who Levels by Shovel," capturing more than 17,800 enemy adherents, taking more than 8,800 heads, and accepting the surrender of more than 13,000 households.
translations.idiomatic: He also crushed Guangdong rebels who called themselves the "King Who Levels with the Shovel," taking more than 17,800 of their followers, more than 8,800 heads, and the submission of more than 13,000 households.

sentences.zh: 還，賜彩幣、上尊、良馬。

translations.literal: On his return he was granted colored silks, imperial wine, and fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he received colored silks, imperial wine, and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 其冬出理山西軍務，巡撫北邊。

translations.literal: That winter he went out to handle Shanxi military affairs and inspect the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was sent to manage Shanxi military affairs and tour the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以左參將從傅友德討納哈出。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, as Left Deputy Commander he followed Fu Youde in campaigning against Naghachu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, as Left Deputy Commander, he followed Fu Youde against Naghachu.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以左副將軍從燕王出古北口，降乃兒不花。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, as Left Deputy General he followed the Prince of Yan out through Gubeikou and received the surrender of Nayirbuqa.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, as Left Deputy General, he marched with the Prince of Yan through Gubeikou and accepted the surrender of Nayirbuqa.

sentences.zh: 還，坐胡惟庸黨死。

translations.literal: On his return, he was executed as an associate of Hu Weiyong.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was put to death as a partisan of Hu Weiyong.

sentences.zh: 爵除。

translations.literal: His nobility was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His title was struck off.

sentences.zh: 楊璟，合肥人。

translations.literal: Yang Jing was a man of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jing was a native of Hefei.

sentences.zh: 本儒家子。

translations.literal: By origin he was a Confucian scholar's son.
translations.idiomatic: He came from a Confucian family.

sentences.zh: 以管軍萬戶從太祖下集慶，進總管。

translations.literal: As a Guard Commander of Ten Thousand he followed the Taizu in taking Jiqing and was promoted to Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As commander of ten thousand he followed the Taizu in taking Jiqing and was promoted to Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 下常州，進親軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: After reducing Changzhou he was promoted to Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Personal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Changzhou fell he was made Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Personal Guard.

sentences.zh: 從下婺州，遷樞密院判官。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Wuzhou and was transferred to Vice Minister of the Military Affairs Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Wuzhou and was transferred to Vice Minister of the Military Affairs Commission.

sentences.zh: 再從伐漢，以功擢湖廣行省參政，移鎮江陵。

translations.literal: Again he followed the campaign against Han and for merit was promoted to Vice Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat, moving his base to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He again campaigned against Han and, for merit, was made Vice Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat and moved his headquarters to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 進攻湖南蠻寇，駐師三江口。

translations.literal: He advanced against Hunan barbarian raiders and encamped his army at Sanjiangkou.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against Hunan tribal raiders and encamped at Sanjiangkou.

sentences.zh: 復以招討功遷行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Again for pacification merit he was transferred to Branch Secretariat Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: For further pacification merit he was made Branch Secretariat Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 帥左丞周德興、參政張彬將武昌諸衛軍，取廣西。

translations.literal: He led Left Chancellor Zhou Dexing and Vice Administrator Zhang Bin with the armies of the Wuchang guards to take Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He led Zhou Dexing, Left Chancellor, and Zhang Bin, Vice Administrator, with the Wuchang guard armies to take Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年春進攻永州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first Hongwu year he advanced to attack Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Hongwu year 1 he advanced on Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 守將鄧祖勝迎戰敗，斂兵固守。

translations.literal: The defending general Deng Zusheng met them in battle and was defeated; he gathered his troops and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: The defender Deng Zusheng gave battle and was beaten; he drew in his troops and held the walls.

sentences.zh: 璟進圍之。

translations.literal: Jing advanced and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jing pressed the siege.

sentences.zh: 元兵來援，駐東鄉，倚湘水列七營，軍勢甚盛。

translations.literal: Yuan troops came to relieve the city, encamped at Dongxiang, and along the Xiang River deployed seven camps—their forces were very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan relief troops encamped at Dongxiang and, along the Xiang River, drew up seven camps in a formidable array.

sentences.zh: 璟擊敗之，俘獲千餘人。

translations.literal: Jing defeated them and captured more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jing routed them and took more than a thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 全州守將平章阿思蘭及周文貴再以兵來援，輒遣德興擊敗之。

translations.literal: The defending Pingzhang Asilan of Quanzhou and Zhou Wengui again came with troops to relieve; Jing repeatedly sent Dexing to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: When Asilan, Pingzhang of Quanzhou, and Zhou Wengui marched to relieve the city again, Jing sent Dexing out repeatedly and beat them back.

sentences.zh: 遣千戶王廷取寶慶，德興、彬取全州，略定道州、藍山、桂陽、武岡諸州縣。

translations.literal: He sent the battalion commander Wang Ting to take Shaoyang; Dexing and Bin took Quanzhou; they pacified Daozhou, Lanshan, Guiyang, Wugang, and other prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the battalion commander Wang Ting against Shaoyang; Dexing and Bin took Quanzhou; they reduced Daozhou, Lanshan, Guiyang, Wugang, and the surrounding prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 而永州久不下，令裨將分營諸門，築壘困之，造浮橋西江上，急攻之。

translations.literal: Yet Yongzhou long would not fall; he ordered lieutenant generals to camp at each gate, built ramparts to press the siege, constructed a pontoon bridge on the western river, and attacked urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou still held out; he had his lieutenants camp at every gate, built siege lines, threw a pontoon bridge across the western moat, and pressed the assault.

sentences.zh: 祖勝力盡，仰藥死。

translations.literal: Zusheng's strength was exhausted; he took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zusheng, spent, took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 百戶夏升約降。

translations.literal: The centurion Xia Sheng arranged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The centurion Xia Sheng agreed to open the gates.

sentences.zh: 璟兵逾城入，參政張子賢巷戰，軍潰被執，遂克永州。

translations.literal: Jing's troops crossed the wall and entered; Vice Administrator Zhang Zixian fought in the lanes; his army collapsed and he was captured; Yongzhou was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's men scaled the wall; Vice Administrator Zhang Zixian fought street by street until his force broke and he was seized, and Yongzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 而征南將軍廖永忠、參政硃亮祖亦自廣東取梧州，定潯、貴、郁林。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Pacification-General of the South Liao Yongzhong and Vice Administrator Zhu Liangzu also from Guangdong took Wuzhou and pacified Xun, Gui, and Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the southern expedition commander Liao Yongzhong and Vice Administrator Zhu Liangzu advanced from Guangdong, took Wuzhou, and pacified Xun, Gui, and Yulin.

sentences.zh: 亮祖以兵來會。

translations.literal: Liangzu came with troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzu marched up to join him.

sentences.zh: 進攻靖江不下，璟謂諸將曰：「彼所恃西濠水耳。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Jingjiang, they could not take it; Jing said to the generals: "What they rely on is only the water in the western moat.
translations.idiomatic: The attack on Jingjiang stalled; Jing told his officers, "They depend on nothing but the western moat.

sentences.zh: 決其堤岸，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: Break the dikes and banks, and they will surely be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Break the dikes and the city must fall.

sentences.zh: 乃遣指揮丘廣攻叚口關，殺守堤兵，盡決濠水，築土堤五道，傅於城。

translations.literal: He then sent the commander Qiu Guang to attack Duankou Pass, killed the troops guarding the dikes, fully drained the moat water, built five earthen embankments, and pressed them against the wall.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Commander Qiu Guang against Duankou Pass, killed the dike guards, drained the moat, threw up five earthen ramps, and pushed them against the wall.

sentences.zh: 城中猶固守。

translations.literal: Within the city they still held firm.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders still held out inside.

sentences.zh: 急攻二月，克之，執平章也兒吉尼。

translations.literal: After urgent assault for two months, it was taken; they captured the Pingzhang Yerzhijini.
translations.idiomatic: After two months of fierce assault the city fell; they seized the Pingzhang Yerzhijini.

sentences.zh: 先是張彬攻南關，為守城者所詬，怒欲屠其民。

translations.literal: Earlier when Zhang Bin attacked the southern gate, the defenders taunted him; in anger he wanted to slaughter the populace.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Bin had assaulted the south gate and been mocked by the garrison; enraged, he meant to massacre the people.

sentences.zh: 璟甫入，立下令禁止之，民乃安。

translations.literal: As soon as Jing entered, he immediately issued orders forbidding it, and the people were then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Jing entered at once and forbade it; only then were the people spared.

sentences.zh: 復移師徇郴州，降兩江土官黃英岑、伯顏等，而永忠亦定南寧、象州。

translations.literal: He again moved his army to pacify Chenzhou, received the surrender of the native officials Huang Yingcen and Boyan of the Two Rivers, while Yongzhong also pacified Nanning and Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Chenzhou, received the submission of the Two Rivers native chiefs Huang Yingcen and Boyan, while Yongzhong secured Nanning and Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣西悉平。

translations.literal: Guangxi was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi was wholly pacified.

sentences.zh: 還，與偏將軍湯和從徐達取山西，至澤州，及元平章韓紮兒戰于韓店，敗績。

translations.literal: On his return, with the Deputy General Tang He he followed Xu Da in taking Shanxi; reaching Zezhou, they fought with the Yuan Pingzhang Han Zha'er at Handian and suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he and Deputy General Tang He followed Xu Da into Shanxi; at Zezhou they fought the Yuan Pingzhang Han Zha'er at Handian and were beaten.

sentences.zh: 還，捕唐州亂卒，留鎮南陽。

translations.literal: On his return he captured mutinous soldiers at Tangzhou and remained to garrison Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the way back he rounded up mutineers at Tangzhou and stayed to garrison Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔璟往使于夏。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered on a mission as envoy to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was ordered to Xia as envoy.

sentences.zh: 是時夏主升幼，母彭及諸大臣用事。

translations.literal: At that time the Xia ruler Sheng was young; his mother Peng and various great ministers held power.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler Sheng was still a boy; his mother Peng and the senior ministers ruled in his name.

sentences.zh: 璟既至。

translations.literal: When Jing arrived—
translations.idiomatic: When Jing arrived,

sentences.zh: 數諭升以禍福，俾從入覲。

translations.literal: he repeatedly instructed Sheng on fortune and calamity and urged him to come to court for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: he urged Sheng again and again on the consequences of his choice and pressed him to come to court.

sentences.zh: 升集其下共議。

translations.literal: Sheng gathered his subordinates to deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng called his advisers together to decide.

sentences.zh: 而諸大臣方專恣，不利升歸朝，皆持不可，升亦莫能決。

translations.literal: But the great ministers were then domineering; Sheng's coming to court was not to their advantage—all held it impossible, and Sheng also could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers, entrenched in power, did not want him at court; all said it could not be done, and Sheng could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 璟還，再以書諭升，終不聽。

translations.literal: Jing returned and again wrote to instruct Sheng, but in the end Sheng would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing went home and wrote again, but Sheng would not listen.

sentences.zh: 逾二年而夏亡。

translations.literal: After more than two years Xia perished.
translations.idiomatic: Within two more years Xia was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 璟遷湖廣行省平章。

translations.literal: Jing was transferred to Huguang Branch Secretariat Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was transferred to Grand Counselor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 慈利土官覃垕構諸洞蠻為亂，命帥師往討，連敗之。

translations.literal: The native official of Cili, Tan You, incited the cave barbarians to rebellion; he was ordered to lead troops to suppress them and defeated them repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Tan You, the native official of Cili, stirred the cave tribes to revolt; Jing was ordered against him and beat him again and again.

sentences.zh: 垕詐降，璟使部卒往報，為所執。

translations.literal: Tan feigned surrender; Jing sent a subordinate to report and he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Tan pretended to submit; Jing sent a man to treat with him and the man was taken.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣使讓璟。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent a messenger to reprove Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu sent an envoy to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 璟督戰，士力攻，賊乃遁。

translations.literal: Jing supervised the battle; the troops attacked with force and the bandits then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jing drove the fight himself; the men pressed hard and the rebels broke.

sentences.zh: 三年大封功臣，封璟營陽侯，祿千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: At the great enfeoffment of meritorious ministers in the third year, Jing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yingyang with salary of 1,500 shi and granted an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: At the third-year enfeoffment of the founding ministers he was made Marquis of Yingyang at 1,500 shi with a hereditary iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 四年從湯和伐夏，戰于瞿塘，不利。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Tang He in campaigning against Xia; they fought at Qutang and met with setbacks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed Tang He against Xia; at Qutang Gorge they met defeat.

sentences.zh: 明年充副將軍，從鄧愈討定辰、沅蠻寇。

translations.literal: The next year he served as deputy general and followed Deng Yu in pacifying the barbarian raiders of Chen and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as deputy general, he followed Deng Yu in pacifying the Chen and Yuan tribal raiders.

sentences.zh: 再從大將軍徐達鎮北平，練兵遼東。

translations.literal: Again he followed the Grand General Xu Da in garrisoning Beiping and trained troops in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Grand General Xu Da in garrisoning Beiping and drilling troops in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 十五年八月卒，追封芮國公，諡武信。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifteenth year he died; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ruiguo with the posthumous title Wuxin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the fifteenth year and was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Ruiguo with the posthumous title Wuxin.

sentences.zh: 子通嗣，二十年帥降軍戍雲南，多道亡，降普定指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Tong inherited; in the twentieth year he led surrendered troops to garrison Yunnan; many fled on the march; he was demoted to Commander of Puding.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tong succeeded; in the twentieth year he led surrendered troops to Yunnan, but many deserted on the road and he was reduced to commander at Puding.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，詔書坐璟胡惟庸黨，謂以瞿塘之敗被責，有異謀雲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year an imperial edict charged Jing as an associate of Hu Weiyong, saying that because he was blamed for the defeat at Qutang he harbored a different design.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year an edict made Jing out as Hu Weiyong's partisan, alleging that after the Qutang defeat and the blame laid on him he had turned disloyal.

sentences.zh: 胡美，沔陽人。

translations.literal: Hu Mei was a man of Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Mei was a native of Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 初名廷瑞，避太祖字，易名美。

translations.literal: His original name was Tingrui; to avoid the Taizu's taboo character, he changed his name to Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Tingrui, he changed his name to Mei to avoid the character used in the Taizu's personal name.

sentences.zh: 初仕陳友諒，為江西行省丞相，守龍興。

translations.literal: At first he served Chen Youliang as Grand Counselor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, defending Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered Chen Youliang's service as grand counselor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and held Longxing.

sentences.zh: 太祖既下江州，遣使招諭美。

translations.literal: After the Taizu had taken Jiangzhou, he sent envoys to summon Mei and persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taizu captured Jiangzhou, he sent envoys to summon and persuade Mei.

sentences.zh: 美遣使鄭仁傑詣九江請降，且請無散部曲。

translations.literal: Mei sent the envoy Zheng Renjie to Jiujiang to request surrender, and also asked that his followers not be dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Mei sent Zheng Renjie to Jiujiang to offer surrender and asked that his troops not be broken up.

sentences.zh: 太祖初難之，劉基蹴所坐胡床。

translations.literal: The Taizu at first found this difficult to accept; Liu Ji kicked the folding camp-chair on which he sat.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu hesitated at first; Liu Ji kicked the camp-chair he was sitting on.

sentences.zh: 太祖悟，賜書報曰：「鄭仁傑至，言足下有效順之誠，此足下明達也；

translations.literal: The Taizu understood and sent a letter in reply: "Zheng Renjie has arrived, saying that you bear a sincere wish to submit—this shows your clear judgment;
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu took the point and wrote back: "Zheng Renjie has come and tells me you mean to submit in good faith—that is clear-sighted of you;

sentences.zh: 又恐分散所部，此足下過慮也。

translations.literal: and also that you fear your command will be scattered—this is your excessive anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: and that you fear your command will be broken up—that is needless worry.

sentences.zh: 吾起兵十年，奇才英士，得之四方多矣。

translations.literal: I have raised troops for ten years and gathered rare talent and outstanding men from all quarters in great number.
translations.idiomatic: In ten years of raising armies I have drawn rare talent and outstanding men from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 有能審天時，料事機，不待交兵，挺然委身來者，嘗推赤心以待，隨其才任使之，兵少則益之以兵，位卑則隆之以爵，財乏則厚之以賞，安肯散其部曲，使人自危疑，負來歸之心哉？

translations.literal: Those who can read the times, foresee how affairs will unfold, and before swords are crossed step forward and give themselves up—I have always received them with an open heart, appointed them according to their abilities, added troops when their forces were few, raised rank when their position was low, and lavished rewards when they lacked wealth. How would I disperse their followers and make men doubt for themselves and turn against the heart that brought them to submit?
translations.idiomatic: Men who read the times, foresee how affairs will turn, and before a blow is struck step forward and give themselves to me—I have always met them with an open heart, used them according to their gifts, given troops where they were few, raised rank where it was low, and heaped rewards where they were poor. Why would I break up their commands, set men doubting themselves, and poison the will to come over?

sentences.zh: 且以陳氏諸將觀之，如趙普勝驍勇善戰，以疑見戮。

translations.literal: Moreover, judge by Chen's generals: Zhao Pusheng was valiant in battle, yet because of suspicion he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Judge by Chen's own generals: Zhao Pusheng was bold and skilled in war, yet suspicion brought him to the blade.

sentences.zh: 猜忌若此，竟何所成。

translations.literal: With such jealousy and distrust, what could ever be achieved?
translations.idiomatic: With jealousy like that, what could ever be won?

sentences.zh: 近建康龍灣之役，予所獲長張、梁鉉、彭指揮諸人，用之如故，視吾諸將，恩均義一。

translations.literal: At the recent battle at Longwan near Jianye, Zhang the Elder, Liang Xuan, Commander Peng, and others whom I captured I employ as before; toward my own generals their favor and fair dealing are one.
translations.idiomatic: At the recent fight at Longwan near Jianye, Zhang the Elder, Liang Xuan, Commander Peng, and the rest whom I took I use as before; I treat them with the same favor and fairness as my own commanders.

sentences.zh: 長張破安慶水寨，梁鉉等攻江北，並膺厚賞。

translations.literal: Zhang the Elder broke Anqing's river stockade; Liang Xuan and the rest attacked north of the Yangzi—all received rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang the Elder stormed Anqing's river stockade; Liang Xuan and the others fought north of the Yangzi—all were richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 此數人者，其自視無復生理，尚待之如此，況如足下不勞一卒，以完城來歸者耶？

translations.literal: These men had already given themselves up for dead, yet I still treated them so; how much more one such as you, who brings a whole city over without costing a single soldier?
translations.idiomatic: These men had already written themselves off for dead, yet I still treated them so—how much more should I honor one who surrenders a whole city without costing me a single soldier?

sentences.zh: 得失之機，間不容髮，足下當早為計。」

translations.literal: The moment for gain or loss allows no hair's breadth between—you should decide early."
translations.idiomatic: The moment for gain or loss turns on a hair—you should decide soon.

sentences.zh: 美得書，乃遣康泰至九江來降。

translations.literal: When Mei received the letter, he then sent Kang Tai to Jiujiang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Mei received the letter, he sent Kang Tai to Jiujiang to submit.

sentences.zh: 太祖遂如龍興，至樵舍。

translations.literal: The Taizu then proceeded to Longxing, reaching Qiaoshe.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu then went to Longxing and came as far as Qiaoshe.

sentences.zh: 美以陳氏所授丞相印及軍民糧儲之數來獻，迎謁於新城門。

translations.literal: Mei presented the grand counselor's seal Chen had granted him and accounts of military and civilian grain stores, and went out to meet him at the New City Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Mei presented the grand counselor's seal Chen had given him, together with tallies of military and civilian grain stores, and went out to meet the Taizu at the New City Gate.

sentences.zh: 太祖慰勞之，俾仍舊官。

translations.literal: The Taizu comforted and praised him and let him keep his former office.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu comforted him and let him keep his former post.

sentences.zh: 美之降也，同僉康泰、平章祝宗不欲從，美微言于太祖。

translations.literal: When Mei surrendered, Associate Censor Kang Tai and Grand Counselor Zhu Zong did not wish to follow; Mei dropped a hint to the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Mei submitted, Associate Censor Kang Tai and Grand Counselor Zhu Zong refused to follow; Mei let the Taizu know in guarded words.

sentences.zh: 太祖命將其兵，從徐達征武昌。

translations.literal: The Taizu ordered their troops taken in hand and sent them with Xu Da to campaign against Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu ordered their armies commandeered and sent them with Xu Da against Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 二人果叛，攻陷洪都。

translations.literal: The two men did rebel and stormed Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: The two did rebel and seized Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 達等還兵擊定之。

translations.literal: Xu Da and the others turned back their troops and put down the revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da and the others turned back and crushed the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 祝宗走死，執康泰歸於建康。

translations.literal: Zhu Zong fled and died; Kang Tai was seized and brought to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zong fled to his death; Kang Tai was taken and brought to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 太祖以泰為美甥，赦勿誅。

translations.literal: Because Tai was Mei's nephew, the Taizu pardoned him and did not execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Kang Tai was Mei's nephew, the Taizu spared him from execution.

sentences.zh: 美從征武昌，復與達等帥馬步舟師取淮東，進伐張士誠，下湖州，圍平江，別將取無錫，降莫天祐。

translations.literal: Mei followed the campaign at Wuchang, then again with Xu Da and the others led horse, foot, and river forces to take Huaidong, advanced against Zhang Shicheng, took Huzhou, besieged Pingjiang, and as a separate commander took Wuxi and reduced Mo Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: Mei campaigned at Wuchang, then again with Xu Da and the others led horse, foot, and river forces through Huaidong, marched against Zhang Shicheng, took Huzhou, besieged Pingjiang, and as a separate commander seized Wuxi and brought Mo Tianyou to surrender.

sentences.zh: 師還，加榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 其冬，命為征南將軍，帥師由江西取福建，諭之曰：「汝以陳氏丞相來歸，事吾數年，忠實無過，故命汝總兵取閩。

translations.literal: That winter he was appointed Southern Campaign General, to lead troops from Jiangxi to take Fujian. The Taizu instructed him: "You came over as Chen's grand counselor; you have served me several years with loyalty and without fault, so I appoint you to command the army to take Min.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was made Southern Campaign General and ordered to lead troops from Jiangxi into Fujian. The Taizu told him: "You came over as Chen's grand counselor and have served me these years with loyalty and without fault, so I put you in command to take Min.

sentences.zh: 左丞何文輝為爾副，參政戴德聽調發，二人雖皆吾親近，勿以其故廢軍法。

translations.literal: Left Vice Counselor He Wenhui is your deputy; Grand Counselor Dai De will follow your deployments. Though both are close to me, do not for that reason relax military law.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Counselor He Wenhui is your deputy; Grand Counselor Dai De will answer your deployments. Though both are men close to me, do not for that slacken military law.

sentences.zh: 聞汝嘗攻閩中，宜深知其地利險易。

translations.literal: I hear you once campaigned in Minzhong; you should know well its terrain, advantages, and difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: I hear you have campaigned in Min before—you should know its ground, its strengths, and its hazards.

sentences.zh: 今總大軍攻圍城邑，必擇便宜可否為進退，無失機宜。」

translations.literal: Now that you command a great army besieging cities, you must choose what is expedient—whether to advance or withdraw—and not miss the right moment."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you command a great host against walled towns, choose what is expedient for advance or retreat and do not miss your moment.

sentences.zh: 美遂渡杉關，下光澤，邵武守將李宗茂以城降。

translations.literal: Mei then crossed Shan Pass, took Guangze, and the defending general of Shaowu, Li Zongmao, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Mei crossed Shan Pass and took Guangze; Li Zongmao, the defending general of Shaowu, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 次建陽，守將曹復疇亦降。

translations.literal: Next at Jianyang the defending general Cao Fuchou also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianyang next, the defending general Cao Fuchou submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 進圍建寧，守將同僉達裏麻、參政陳子琦謀堅守以老我師。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Jianning, Associate Censor Dalima and Grand Counselor Chen Ziqi plotted to hold firm and wear down our army.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to besiege Jianning, where Associate Censor Dalima and Grand Counselor Chen Ziqi planned to hold fast and wear our army down.

sentences.zh: 美數挑戰，不出，急攻之，乃降。

translations.literal: Mei repeatedly challenged them to battle; they would not come out; he pressed the assault hard and they surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Mei challenged them again and again, but they would not come out; he pressed the assault hard and they surrendered.

sentences.zh: 整軍入城，秋毫無所犯。

translations.literal: He marched his troops into the city in good order and violated nothing, down to a hair.
translations.idiomatic: He marched his troops into the city in good order and harmed nothing, not even a hair.

sentences.zh: 執子琦等送京師，獲將士九千七百餘人，糧糗馬畜稱是。

translations.literal: Chen Ziqi and the rest were seized and sent to the capital; more than 9,700 officers and soldiers were captured, with grain, fodder, horses, and livestock in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ziqi and the rest were seized and sent to the capital; more than nine thousand seven hundred officers and men were taken, with grain, fodder, horses, and livestock to match.

sentences.zh: 會湯和等亦取福州、延平、興化，美遂遣降將諭降汀、泉諸郡。

translations.literal: When Tang He and the others had also taken Fuzhou, Yanping, and Xinghua, Mei then sent surrendered generals to announce surrender and bring over the prefectures of Ting and Quan.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang He and the others had also taken Fuzhou, Yanping, and Xinghua, Mei sent surrendered generals to proclaim submission and win over the prefectures of Ting and Quan.

sentences.zh: 福建悉平。

translations.literal: Fujian was wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian was wholly pacified.

sentences.zh: 美留守其地。

translations.literal: Mei remained to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: Mei remained to garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 尋召還，從幸汴梁。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned back and accompanied the emperor on a visit to Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled and accompanied the court on its visit to Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：馮勝、傅友德，百戰驍將也。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Feng Sheng and Fu Youde were battle-tested fierce generals.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser writes: Feng Sheng and Fu Youde were generals hardened in a hundred fights.

sentences.zh: 考當日功臣位次，與太祖褒美之詞，豈在湯和、鄧愈下哉。

translations.literal: Considering the ranking of meritorious ministers of the day and the Taizu's words of praise, how could they rank below Tang He and Deng Yu?
translations.idiomatic: Weigh their standing among the founding ministers of the day and the Taizu's words of praise—how could they rank below Tang He and Deng Yu?

sentences.zh: 廖永忠智勇超邁，功亞宋、潁，皆不得以功名終，身死爵除，為可慨矣。

translations.literal: Liao Yongzhong's wisdom and courage surpassed the common run; his merit was second only to the Song and Ying [dukes], yet none of them ended in merit and fame; they died and their titles were extinguished—how lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yongzhong's wisdom and courage stood above the common run; his merit was second only to the dukes of Song and Ying—yet none of them finished their lives in merit and fame; they died and their titles were struck away. How lamentable.

sentences.zh: 江夏侯周德興之得罪也，太祖宥之，因誡諭公、侯，謂多粗暴無禮，自取敗亡。

translations.literal: When Marquis of Jiangxia Zhou Dexing was charged with an offense, the Taizu pardoned him and thereby admonished the dukes and marquises, saying many were crude, violent, and without decorum and brought ruin on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis of Jiangxia Zhou Dexing fell under accusation, the Taizu pardoned him and used the occasion to warn the dukes and marquises that many were crude, violent, and without decorum and had brought ruin on themselves.

sentences.zh: 又謂永忠數犯法，屢宥不悛。

translations.literal: He also said Yongzhong had broken the law many times and, though repeatedly pardoned, would not reform.
translations.idiomatic: He also said Yongzhong had broken the law again and again and, though repeatedly spared, would not mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 然則洪武功臣之不獲保全者，或亦有以自取歟。

translations.literal: Thus among the founding ministers of the Hongwu reign, those who could not preserve themselves to the end may in part also have brought it on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: So among the Hongwu founding ministers, those who could not keep themselves safe to the end may in part have had only themselves to blame.

sentences.zh: 楊璟、胡美功雖不逮，然嘗別將，各著方面勳，故次列之雲。

translations.literal: Yang Jing and Hu Mei, though their merit did not reach such heights, each once commanded as a separate general and won distinguished service in their regions, and so they are placed next in order—as this record shows.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jing and Hu Mei, though their merit did not match this, each once led armies on his own and won notable service in his region; they are therefore set down here in the next rank—as the foregoing shows.
